findings.title: Two photos with the same file name overwrite each other's project: the first project's art and sidecar are replaced
findings.statement: The first Generate builds its output folder from the photo's file name alone (out = <parent>/<image-stem>-field) and never checks whether that folder already holds a project. image-field then writes art/base.png, walkmesh.obj and <stem>.trace.json into it unconditionally, because only the toml path depends on the Name. So a second, unrelated photo that has the same file name (phone exports IMG_0001.jpg, image.png, photo.jpg) silently replaces the first project's background art, walkmesh and session record. The first project's own field.toml survives and now points at the other room's art. Reopening it in Trace loads the OTHER session (the sidecar glob picks the overwritten <stem>.trace.json), so the next Regenerate writes the other project's name and id.
findings.evidence: Script: probes/x-trace-e2e/p3_reopen_crosstab.py, section D. Output is in p3.out next to it. Setup: phoneA/IMG_0001.jpg (800x600) is generated as CELLAR id 30120 into projects/, and a hand [[npc]] Bob is added. Then phoneB/IMG_0001.jpg (600x800, a different photo) is generated as ATTIC id 30121 into the same parent. Output: 'D files: [ATTIC.field.toml, CELLAR.field.toml, IMG_0001.trace.json, art/base.png, walkmesh.obj]', 'D CELLAR files overwritten: [art/base.png, IMG_0001.trace.json]', 'D sidecar now names: ATTIC ...phoneB\IMG_0001.jpg', 'D reopen CELLAR.field.toml in Trace -> name box ATTIC id 30121'. walkmesh.obj was only spared because both traces used the same clicks; with a different trace it is overwritten too (build_image_field writes it unconditionally, imagefield.py:1108). Exit 0, no warning anywhere.
findings.user_path: Trace a phone photo IMG_0001.jpg into Documents/ and Generate. Later, trace a different IMG_0001.jpg from another day and pick Documents/ again. Project 1's background is now the second photo.
findings.fix: On a FIRST Generate, refuse an existing <stem>-field folder or suffix it (-field-2). Reuse a folder only when its .trace.json names the same image path, or when the user confirms. Name the sidecar after the project Name or id, not the photo stem, so two sessions cannot share one record.
findings.note: Re-checked by the lead in source: `tracedoc.py:833` builds the folder from the photo stem alone and nothing checks that it is free.

findings.title: A pending Editor form folds into the wrong row after a Place delete or reshape
findings.statement: Switching to the Place tab does not commit the Editor form that is still mounted (_on_tab_changed only calls _feed_place). _on_place_edit (shell.py:5143) records the Place op but leaves _save_ctx alone, and _save_ctx still holds the old list index. At the next fold (any tree navigation, Save via _ensure_saved, or Undo/Redo, which all go through _commit_active_ck), _commit_active (shell.py:7582-7621) pops every spec key from lst[ctx['idx']] and writes the form's values there. Example: the author edits gateway g1's form and does not navigate away, then deletes g0 on Place. The fold now writes g1's edited values over g2, so g2 is destroyed and g1 appears twice. If the deleted row was the last one, idx >= len and the author's edit is silently dropped. If the author reshapes the same gateway on Place instead, the fold writes the form's old zone back over the drag. The trigger needs an unsaved, actually changed form (an untouched form folds to a no-op), but nothing in the UI warns about it, and the result is lost data written into the user's toml.
findings.evidence: Read shell.py 4955-5013, 5143-5169, 5378-5395 and 7582-7621. _checkpoint never touches _save_ctx, and only delete/remove paths (5635, 5666, 7317) clear it. I re-ran place-code/p6_shell.py on the real Workspace (offscreen, prefs and config pinned). Output: 'mounted form: gateway:1 idx 1' / 'after Place delete: [(g1,101),(g2,102)]' / 'after the Editor fold: [(g1,101,[200,0]),(g1,555,[200,0])]', so g2 is gone. The probe simulates the edit by swapping the form getter rather than typing into the widget. That is equivalent, because _commit_active only reads the getters.
findings.user_path: Editor: open gateway 1, change 'to', do not click elsewhere -> Place tab -> Load -> Regions -> right-click gateway 0 -> Delete -> click any tree node or Save.
findings.fix: Commit the active form when the Place (and Cutscene/Behavior) tab is shown: call _commit_active_ck() in _on_tab_changed before _feed_place. If the commit fails (invalid value), stay on the Editor or drop _save_ctx and remount. As a safety net, _on_place_edit should set _save_ctx=None (or remount the form) when the mutated section equals ctx['section'].

findings.title: First Regenerate that adds a region deletes Place-minted door0/zone0
findings.statement: is_generated_region() decides that a project is 'legacy' because it has no traced_ row. A project generated by the current code with no regions also has no traced_ rows, so it looks legacy too. The earlier fix (allow_legacy=False when the session emits no regions) only covers a regenerate that still has no regions. It does not cover the moment the author first adds one. The flow: Trace a floor and Generate. In Place, draw a gateway or event; placedoc._fresh_name mints 'door0'/'zone0'. Back in Trace, draw any region and Regenerate. The merge claims the hand door0/zone0 as the generator's and deletes them. The deletion appears only as a 'removed' line in the CLI output in the Output panel. The load_project absorb path (tracedoc.py:1017, allow_legacy defaults to True) has the same misclassification. However, it only runs for projects with no .trace.json sidecar (CLI-generated or pre-sidecar). GUI-generated projects always take load_trace, so that half of the claim is narrower than reported.
findings.evidence: Re-ran the reporter's probe_build.py as a copy in my scratch dir, with PYTHONPATH pinned to the worktree package. 'regen no-regions: removed [] kept [... '[[gateway]] door0', '[[event]] zone0']' then 'regen +event: removed ['[[gateway]] door0', '[[event]] zone0']'; 'gateways now: [] events: ['traced_zone0']'. Confirmed placedoc.py:97-126 mints door0/zone0. test_imagefield.py:707 pins only the no-regions case; test :596 covers a project that already has traced_ rows. Nothing covers the no-regions to regions transition. PLAN.md:467 records the earlier fix as closing this class, but it did not.
findings.user_path: Trace a floor, Generate. Place tab: draw a gateway (door0). Trace tab: draw one event zone, then Regenerate. The Place door is gone from the field.toml.
findings.fix: The sidecar-marker idea does not help CLI projects. Better: retire the legacy branch, or gate it on a durable marker the generator writes, for example a top-level 'generator = "image-field/2"' scalar (scalars ride through the merge). The cost of a missed legacy claim is one visible duplicated door; the cost of a false claim is silent data loss. Pass the same decision to load_project's absorb. Add a regression test for the no-regions to regions transition.

findings.title: Trace Regenerate does not refresh the open FieldDoc; a later Save All overwrites the regenerated toml
findings.statement: The first Trace Generate opens the project through on_generated=open_field. Later Regenerates rewrite the same field.toml in place, but _after_generate returns early when first is False, so the shell's FieldDoc buffer (and the Place tab that shares it) keeps the pre-regenerate data. FieldDoc.save and shell._save_all do no disk-drift or mtime check. Any later Place drop, Cutscene edit or form edit marks the stale buffer dirty, and Save All writes it over the regenerated toml. The Trace-drawn gateways and events disappear, and [camera] reverts to the old pose while walkmesh.obj and the art stay regenerated, so camera and walkmesh no longer match. This happens even when the author saved everything before regenerating; the reporter's probe ordering (dirty before the regenerate, plus --force) is not needed. The reverse also holds: a Regenerate merges from disk, so unsaved Place edits made before it are not seen and are later re-saved without the new regions.
findings.evidence: My probe p_t38.py (offscreen, prefs and LOCALAPPDATA pinned to scratch): open_field on the generated toml, then an in-place regenerate through the same CLI the tab runs, WITHOUT --force, adding --gateway. Output: 'disk after regen: gateways 1', 'place buffer gateways: 0', then after one Place NPC drop and _save_all: 'disk after Place drop + Save All: gateways 0 npcs 1'. grep shows no QFileSystemWatcher or mtime check on member tomls in shell.py, and editor/model.py save() has none.
findings.user_path: Trace a photo, Generate (the project opens). Trace tab: draw a gateway and Regenerate. Place tab: drop an NPC. Save All. The gateway is gone from the toml.
findings.fix: After every clean Generate whose toml is the shell's open member, reload it: reopen if the buffer is clean, ask (keep mine / take regenerated) if it is dirty. Better, make Trace's Generate refuse or prompt while that member has unsaved edits, since the merge reads disk. As a backstop, record the mtime and size at load in FieldDoc and have save()/_save_all refuse or ask when the file changed on disk.

findings.title: Staging verdicts from every scene paint on whichever scene is selected
findings.statement: cutscenescan.stage_verdicts returns verdict rows for every cast [[cutscene]] block, each tagged with 'scene'. _finish_stage hands all of them to canvas.set_verdicts, and CutsceneStage._draw paints every row (red leg, ring and 'step N stalls here') without comparing v['scene'] with the selected scene. _pts also adds those foreign points to the fit bounds. In a dispatch, a stall in scene #1 is drawn on scene #0's stage at scene #0's 'step 0', which is a different step that is fine, so the author is pointed at the wrong step. Switching scenes does not re-filter, because the rows persist across redraws by design.
findings.evidence: Re-ran cutscene-code/p3_verdicts.py, a valid probe that drives the public stage_now(sync=True) with rail row 0 selected. Output: 'summary: 1 staging problem across 2 scenes', 'scene#0 selected; verdict rows: [(1, 0)]', canvas tags include verdict: 2, and the stall label 'step 0 stalls here' is drawn on scene #0's stage. The code read agrees: _draw at lines 197-204 has no scene filter. No test pins painting other scenes' verdicts.
findings.user_path: A field with a [[cutscene]] dispatch of 2 or more cast scenes; scene #1 has a blocked walk. Select scene #0, press Check the staging, and the red stall marker paints on scene #0.
findings.fix: Keep the full rows on the doc, and pass only the selected scene's rows to the canvas: canvas.set_verdicts([r for r in rows if r['scene'] == self._scene]). Re-apply that filter in _render and _on_scene_select. Add a fence using a two-cast-scene fixture.

findings.title: Undo/redo leaves the open step editor aimed at a stale index; Apply overwrites another step or raises
findings.statement: Shell _apply_history swaps in a restored deep copy of the document and re-feeds the Cutscene doc. show_field decides 'same field' by member name alone, so it never runs _close_editor, and editor.scene, step_i, insert_at and the widget contents all survive into the restored document. The next Apply calls update_step(self._raw, self._scene, editor.step_i, ...) on the new data, which does one of two things. (a) If the index now holds a different step, Apply silently overwrites it with the editor's stale content: one step is destroyed and another is duplicated. (b) If the index no longer exists, it raises IndexError out of a Qt slot, and the user sees Apply do nothing. _apply_step also uses self._scene rather than editor.scene. The damage is itself undoable, but it is silent: the editor still shows the old content as if nothing had changed.
findings.evidence: Re-ran both reporter probes; both drive the real shell Workspace._undo(), which is the Ctrl+Z path, so they are valid. p2_lifecycle.py: 'A after undo: editor target 0 3 steps 3' -> 'A APPLY RAISED IndexError list index out of range'; in A2 the turn step at index 1 is replaced by the say, and the say is now duplicated at steps 1 and 2. shell-lifecycle/probe1.py: after move ['B','A'], editor on step 0 shows 'B'; after undo ['A','B'] the editor is still on 0 showing 'B'; after Apply the steps are ['B','B'], so 'A' is lost.
findings.user_path: Cutscene tab: open the pencil editor on a step, or Add a step, then press Ctrl+Z (or Redo) while the editor is still open, then press Apply.
findings.fix: In show_field, when raw is not self._raw (an undo, redo or reload), call _close_editor() and clear _selected_step if it is now out of range. Also make _apply_step use editor.scene and bounds-check step_i, showing a note in the editor on a mismatch instead of writing.

findings.title: Undo/redo never re-judges the armed staging, leaving a stale tick over a restored stall
findings.statement: Once the staging lane is armed (after the first explicit check), the automatic re-judge starts only from _after_edit and _on_scene_select. A same-field re-feed through show_field re-renders but never starts _restage_timer. Undo, redo and edits made in other tabs (for example a Place-tab NPC move) all arrive that way. After the user fixes a stall (the note turns to a tick and the verdicts clear) and presses Ctrl+Z, the document contains the stalling walk again, but the instruments still say every walk reaches its target and nothing is painted on the stage.
findings.evidence: Re-ran p8_undo_restage.py, which uses the real shell _undo. Output: '1 stall: 1 staging problem', '2 fixed: Every walk ... verdicts 0', '3 after undo: doc walk = [2000, 2000] | restage timer armed: False | note: Every walk in 1 scene reaches its target. | verdicts 0'. Code read: show_field (lines 980-1003) has no _restage_timer.start().
findings.user_path: Check the staging, fix a stall, then press Ctrl+Z.
findings.fix: In show_field's same-field path, start _restage_timer when self._stage_armed and self._wmesh is not None. That covers undo, redo and cross-tab re-feeds. It is cheap, because the timer debounces and runs on the worker.

findings.title: The warm staging walkmesh is never invalidated: an explicit re-check uses a stale mesh, even another project's
findings.statement: stage_now always passes the cached self._wmesh to the worker, and the walkmesh is loaded from disk only when that cache is None. The cache is cleared only by _reset_stage, which runs only when the member NAME changes in show_field, or on show_none. open_field and open_campaign never call show_none. This has two effects. (1) After the field's walkmesh is changed on disk (a Trace regenerate, a Blender re-export, a new bgi), even an explicit 'Check the staging' click judges against the old mesh, although the tooltip says the walkmesh comes from the SAVED file. (2) Opening a different project whose member has the same name (a copied field, or a re-import of the same fork) keeps the previous project's mesh, so the new project's walks are judged, and the storyboard is routed, on the wrong floor. The armed flag carries over too. In both cases the verdict is confidently wrong. The behavior tab's sweep cache (behaviordoc._wmesh) has the same shape.
findings.evidence: Re-ran p4_meshcache.py. Same doc after the bgi was replaced on disk: 'explicit re-check after the mesh changed on disk: Every walk...', while 'fresh doc on the same file: 1 staging problem'. Shell: GLEN opened from sa and checked, then GLEN opened from sb: 'armed True mesh id <same id>', 'shell B check: Every walk...' (a fresh load warns). Note: shell-lifecycle/probe2.py does prove that the cached mesh object is reused, but in my run its 'truth after forced reset' line also printed a tick, so that probe does not by itself show a wrong verdict. p4 does.
findings.user_path: Check the staging, then either regenerate or re-export the walkmesh and check again, or open another project that has a same-named member and check.
findings.fix: Reset the stage when path != self._path (not only when the member changes), and have the button's click path pass wmesh=None so an explicit check always reloads. Keep the warm mesh for automatic re-judges only. Optionally key the cache on (path, walkmesh mtime). Apply the same fix to behaviordoc's sweep cache.

findings.title: Applying a step with an int style rewrites it as a string the build rejects
findings.statement: open_step shows style = 128 as the text '128', and read_step writes every non-blank speaker, tail or style back as a string. content.text.resolve_style accepts an int flags byte but treats any string as a style NAME, so '128' fails with "unknown window style '128'". style is an editor-managed key, so any Apply of such a step corrupts it, even one that only fixes a typo in the line. Typing a raw byte into the Window style box, as its own tooltip invites ('a raw flags byte'), also produces a value the build rejects. The build refuses the field, so no bad bytes ship, but the editor breaks a valid document and offers no way to enter the documented int form.
findings.evidence: Re-ran p1_roundtrip.py, which drives the public _edit_step/_apply_step: step 0 BEFORE {'say':'Hi','style':128} AFTER {'say':'Hi','style':'128'}, and resolve_style then raises 'unknown window style '128' ... or a raw flags byte 0..255'. Read content/text.py:61-76, which confirms that only an int counts as a flags byte.
findings.user_path: A say step with style = 128 (hand-written, or as the tooltip suggests): open it in the step editor and press Apply.
findings.fix: In read_step, convert an all-digit style to int and leave anything else as a name. Add style=128 to the editor round-trip test.

findings.title: ElideButton elides its own label at its own sizeHint ('＋ St…', '⧉ Sce…' at 100%)
findings.statement: ElideButton.sizeHint returns int(QFontMetrics.horizontalAdvance(full)) + pad, which truncates the fractional advance. _elide then calls elidedText(full, ElideRight, width - pad), which measures at sub-pixel precision. A button laid out at exactly its own hint therefore elides whenever the true advance has a fraction above the integer. In the Cutscene scene bar the buttons sit at hint width. At 100% this turns the primary '＋ Step' into '＋ St…' and '⧉ Scene' into '⧉ Sce…' in every theme. '− Scene' breaks at 125%, '⧉ Scene' at 150%, and 'Storyboard' at 125%/1024. The published docsite figure (editor-cutscene_light.png) shows '+ St…' and 'Sce…'. One reporter's extension to ElideLabel/NameLabel (widgets.py:433/:508) is WRONG: those use int + 2 in both the hint and the elide width, and the 2px slack absorbs the fraction. Measured natively, ElideLabels at their hint show the full text.
findings.evidence: My native probe (v-cutscene-ux/elide.py: real ElideButtons, role=quiet, app QSS, WA_DontShowOnScreen, in a 1400px host with a stretch): "'＋ Step'->'＋ St…' w79 hint79 f45.08", "'⧉ Scene'->'⧉ Sce…' w88 hint88 f54.31", while 'Settings' and '− Scene' were full. A patched sizeHint using ceil(QFontMetricsF advance) + 1 gave '＋ Step', '⧉ Scene' and '− Scene' all in full (v-cutscene-ux/elide2.py). The same probe showed ElideLabel at its hint unelided ('＋ Step' -> '＋ Step'). Snaps mist-100/cutscene-doc-pane and dracula-125-w1024 staged match.
findings.user_path: Open any field with a cutscene on the Cutscene tab at the default window: the add-step button reads '＋ St…' and Duplicate scene reads 'Sce…'.
findings.fix: In ElideButton.sizeHint use math.ceil(QFontMetricsF(self.font()).horizontalAdvance(self._full)) + 1 + self._pad(), and/or have _elide short-circuit to the full text when the float advance is <= w. Add a native gui_snap or test assertion that an ElideButton at its own sizeHint shows text() == accessibleName(). ElideLabel needs no change.

findings.title: The 'Set flag' step accepts a reserved, save-corrupting bit and every GUI check stays clean
findings.statement: The step editor's 'Set flag (idx, val)' kind is typed as a PAIR (forms.py:365), so it takes only two integers. It refuses a [[flag]] name, even though the build resolves names on set_flag. It accepts any index, including 8600, which flags.is_reserved reports as reserved (the read-mail payload band, here the kit's deathrules outpost word). No GUI surface catches it: the tab's PROBLEMS lane (dispatch_problems + scene_problems) has no band check, and the Workspace Check (_check_loose) runs only validate + lint_logic. Only lint_flag_bands catches it, and that is lint-only and reached only through the CLI lint action. A deploy would write a save-corrupting bit with every GUI readout green. A mitigating factor: the step hint does say 'custom flags live in 8712+'. Other forms in the same file use FLAGPAIR, which takes names.
findings.evidence: My probe v-cutscene-bugs/flag.py: with set_flag [8600,1], validate -> [], lint_logic -> [], tab -> [], while lint_flag_bands -> 'writes story flag 8600, inside FF9's reserved ... region -- writing here corrupts real save/engine state'. forms.make_step('set_flag','chest_potion, 1') -> 'pair: must be whole numbers', while build.validate accepts {'set_flag': ['chest_potion', 1]} with a [[flag]] def. Grep: there is no lint_flag_bands/lint_all call under workspace/ or editor/.
findings.user_path: Cutscene step editor: Type 'Set flag', value '8600, 1', Apply, then Check and Deploy, all clean.
findings.fix: Switch the cutscene step kind to FLAGPAIR so names resolve, like the other forms. Add an is_reserved check on raw set_flag indices to scene_problems and the editor's read_step note. Consider having the Workspace's _check_loose include lint_flag_bands.

findings.title: Step-editor wrap preview disagrees with the build: markup, speaker name and quotes, and literal \n
findings.statement:
The step editor's 'On-screen preview — how it wraps in the FF9 window' wraps the raw typed text. The build wraps with_speaker(speaker, text) (build.py ~9474), which first expands {colour} markup to zero-width tags, adds the speaker's name line and wraps the body in curly quotes, and the editor's own read_step turns a typed '
' into a newline. So the preview breaks lines in different places, leaves out the name line, and shows '
' literally, even though the field's tooltip says '
' works. The same text feeds the '✓ fits the window' overflow note, so that note can be wrong too.
findings.evidence: Probe probes/x-cutscene-place/p9_wrap.py (native Qt, real Workspace, narration scene, editor open on its say step). Each case compares the preview box with the build's own with_speaker+wrap_text: markup PREVIEW ['You obtained the {item}Ancient','Mythril Ore of the Lost Northern','Kingdom{/} at last, well done.'] vs BUILD ['You obtained the [C8B040][HSHD]Ancient Mythril','Ore of the Lost Northern Kingdom[C8C8C8][HSHD] at','last, well done.']; speaker=Cid PREVIEW ['We crossed the whole glen before','the dusk light faded out over'] vs BUILD ['Cid','“We crossed the whole glen before','the dusk light faded out over”']; literal \n PREVIEW ['First line here\\nSecond line'] vs BUILD ['First line here','Second line'].
findings.user_path: Cutscene tab → Edit a say step → type a line with a Speaker name (extras drawer), a {item}…{/} colour, or a '\n' → read the preview
findings.fix: Have the panel preview what the build emits: wrap_preview(with_speaker(x_speaker.text(), text.replace('\\n','\n')), ww). Re-run the preview when the speaker field changes. Do the same in the storyboard's _show_beat.

findings.title: 'Pick on the stage' stays armed after Apply or after editing another row, and takes over the next stage press
findings.statement: _arm_stage_pick shows no sign that it is armed: the cursor stays OpenHand, the hint text does not change, and no status appears. Only _close_editor or a pick disarms it. Apply leaves it armed, and so does Edit on another row (open_step never disarms). While it is armed, StageCanvas.mousePressEvent sends the left press to the pick before the edit-handle drag can start. A later press on the walk-target handle, or a click to pan, is consumed: the drag never happens and the editor's value is silently replaced with the pressed coordinates. When the editor is on a say step, the pick writes into the hidden value line, and that phantom value appears if the step type is switched to walk. The pick also accepts points far off the walkmesh (3001, 3001 on a mesh of x -300..1000, z -300..600) with no note, and PROBLEMS still reads 'No structural problems.'
findings.evidence: Probe probes/x-cutscene-place/p3_anim_pick.py: 'after Apply: sim armed? True editor open True step_i 0'. Then a real QTest press, move and release on the handle: 'handle drag while armed: step0 before {'walk': 'altar', ...} after {'walk': 'altar', ...} editor value now '900, 399''. Arming and then Edit on row 2: 'after Edit row 2 (say): armed True', a stage click gives value_line '0, 0', and 'switch say->walk: value_line '0, 0''. p2_stage.py: 'cursor after arm CursorShape.OpenHandCursor hint Ctrl+scroll zooms · Ctrl+0 fits'; 'off-mesh picked -> '3001, 3001' note ''' then 'after apply step0 = {'walk': [3001, 3001] ...} problems: No structural problems.'
findings.user_path: Cutscene tab → Edit a walk step → Pick on the stage → Apply without picking (or Edit another row) → later drag the walk-target handle or click the stage to pan
findings.fix: Disarm in _apply_step, in open_step/_edit_step/_add_step and in _on_kind. While armed, show a crosshair cursor and swap the hint to 'click the stage to pick · Esc cancels', and give the pick button a checked state. Have _stage_picked report when the point lies off the warm walkmesh.

findings.title: After Close project, another project with the same field name shows the old project's '✓ Every walk reaches its target'
findings.statement: _close_project never resets the Cutscene doc: it keeps _member, _raw, _path, the warm walkmesh and the staging note. An in-flight check also lands after the close. When the next opened project has a member with the same name, show_field treats it as same_field (it compares by member name only), so nothing resets. The inspector then shows the previous project's verdict, '✓ Every walk in 1 scene reaches its target.', over a field whose walk is actually blocked. It stays until the user presses Check again. C4 covers the stale mesh on a re-check; this is the verdict itself carrying over with no re-check, caused by Close not resetting the doc.
findings.evidence: Probe probes/x-cutscene-place/p4b_same_name.py: 'P1 verdict: ✓ Every walk in 1 scene reaches its target.' → win._close_project() → 'after close: doc member GLEN raw None? False wmesh kept True note ✓ Every walk…' → open a second GLEN project whose walk goes to [2000,2000] → 'P2 opened (blocked walk), no Check pressed: path cut2b | note: ✓ Every walk in 1 scene reaches its target.' The true verdict is 'P2 cold truth: ⚠ 1 staging problem across 1 scene.' p4_stage_timing.py also showed a check that was in flight across Close landing afterwards, with no exception.
findings.user_path: Open a field → Cutscene → Check the staging (✓) → Close project → open another project whose field has the same name → Cutscene tab
findings.fix: Call cutscene_doc.show_none() (and place_doc.show_none()) from _close_project. In show_field, treat a member as the same field only when both the name and the path match.
findings.note: Same root as C4 (the staging state survives a project close and reopen).

findings.title: Multi-camera [walkmesh] auto field: Place under camera 1+ checks clicks against a different walkmesh than the build ships
findings.statement: build_surface_from_project resolves the walkmesh with the selected camera (resolve_walkmesh(project, cams[ci])). The build always frames it with camera 0 (resolve_camera, 'the primary camera drives the walkmesh frame'). For an auto-framed walkmesh the two meshes differ. Under camera 1, Place accepts clicks on a floor the game will not have, and refuses parts of the real one. Content placed this way lands off the shipped walkmesh with no warning in the tab.
findings.evidence: Probe probes/x-cutscene-place/p7_multicam.py: a composed room rewritten with two [[camera]] blocks. '[auto] BUILD mesh extent (-1215, 1215, -1924, 256)'; 'Place cam 0: … same as build: True'; 'Place cam 1: extent (-843, 843, -1846, 322) same as build: False'. With [walkmesh] obj both cameras match. p8_multicam_gui.py drove the real tab: cam_box set to 1, then a real click at world z=300 gives 'place NPC dali_sweeper at (2, 307) · floor 0', which is beyond the shipped mesh's max z of 256.
findings.user_path: Place tab on a novel field with several [[camera]] blocks and walkmesh auto → Camera combo → camera 1 → click near the far edge
findings.fix: Resolve the surface mesh with cams[0] (as the build does) and project it through cams[ci] only for display and the raycast.

findings.title: image-field crashes on its success print for any non-cp1252 character, so a fully written project is reported as 'failed (exit 1)'
findings.statement: _cmd_image_field prints the toml path, the event messages (via repr) and the deploy hint AFTER build_image_field has written every file. It never calls the house _safe_console() guard. Under the Workspace's QProcess, stdout is a pipe in the locale codepage (cp1252 on Windows), so these characters raise UnicodeEncodeError and the process exits 1 with a traceback: an arrow or CJK text in an event message, or a non-cp1252 character in the photo or output path (for example a Polish, Czech, Cyrillic or CJK Windows user name, since the installed default output folder is ~/Dream World IX). The tab then shows 'Image -> field -- failed (exit 1)' with a hint blaming a vertex above the horizon or the Int16 bound. The first-Generate hand-off to the Editor/Place is skipped, yet the project on disk is complete and correct. Not covered by T8, which is about what a failure does to the tab's state; this is a failure that is not a failure.
findings.evidence: Full shell, real QProcess run_job, child env without PYTHONUTF8 or PYTHONIOENCODING. Script: probes/x-trace-e2e/p6_shell_cp1252.py (output in p6.out): event zone message 'Go \u2192 north', first Generate. Output: files [HALL.field.toml, art, base.png, hall.trace.json, walkmesh.obj]; Problems: 'Image -> field -- failed (exit 1) -- See the Output panel -- the usual causes are a vertex above the horizon or a floor larger than the Int16 world bound.'; '1. first Generate: editor tab = Trace | member_paths []' (no hand-off). Same result from the tab-level probe p3_reopen_crosstab.py section C: 'C exit 1 handed [] ... UnicodeEncodeError: charmap codec can't encode character \u2192'. Same result from the CLI with a CJK photo folder, p1b.out: exit=1 after T.field.toml, art and walkmesh.obj were written.
findings.user_path: Draw an event zone whose message contains an arrow, a dash beyond cp1252, or Japanese, OR have a non-Latin-1 Windows user name and use the default output folder. Click Generate.
findings.fix: Call _safe_console() at the top of _cmd_image_field, as the dialogue verbs do. Better: have run_job set PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8 (or PYTHONUTF8=1) in the QProcess environment and decode the output as UTF-8, so every CLI verb the Workspace streams is covered.
findings.note: Re-checked by the lead in source: `_cmd_image_field` never calls `_safe_console()` and the job runner sets no `PYTHONIOENCODING`.

findings.title: Place ignores the sibling scene.toml: its spawn/arrival/zone edits are overridden at build and scene-owned content is invisible
findings.statement: _feed_place passes only fd.data, the raw field.toml, to PlaceDoc. build._merge_scene (build.py:164-188) overlays a sibling <stem>.scene.toml in which the scene wins per key for [player] (spawn, arrival) and for same-named npc/gateway/event/marker rows; camera, walkmesh and layers come entirely from the scene. So on a Blender-split field: (1) a Spawn/Arrival click writes field.toml, the status confirms it and the marker moves, but the build still ships the scene.toml value; (2) dragging a zone or NPC that the scene names changes nothing at build; (3) scene-only entities are never drawn and are missing from _fresh_name's taken set, so a new 'door0' silently inherits the scene's 'door0' zone; (4) own_scene = bool(data.get('layers')) misses layers that live only in scene.toml, so such a fork is placed against the donor's art. The Cutscene tab already gets merged_fn=fd.merged (shell.py:5085); Place does not. Props are not affected because 'prop' is not in _ENTITY_LISTS. PLAN.md:643 records the scene override only as a known issue of the floorplan recompose, not as a Place decision.
findings.evidence: Read build.py 103-188 and shell.py 5156-5169/5085. I re-ran place-ux-look/probe1.py section 4: 'field.toml spawn after Place: [400, 900] -> build sees: [-100, -100]', 'arrival ... [50,60] -> build sees [7,7]', while the markers drawn were at (400,900)/(50,60). I re-ran place-code/p2_ops.py: region_rows shows 'door0 → 70' at the drawn quad, but BUILD gateways show door0 at the scene's [[500,500],...] zone.
findings.user_path: A field exported from the Blender add-on (field.toml + scene.toml) -> Place -> Load -> click Spawn / draw a gateway -> Save -> build/deploy: the shipped field uses the scene.toml values.
findings.fix: Feed Place fd.merged (as Cutscene does) for markers, regions, own_scene and the fresh-name taken set. Refuse edits to scene-owned keys with the Editor's 'Placed in Blender' wording (spawn/arrival when scene has [player], rows whose name the scene defines), or write those keys to the scene file. Refusing is the smaller change. Note that ops must keep mutating fd.data, not the merged copy.

findings.title: _project_backdrop ignores layer position/size/camera and shrinks the composite to each later layer
findings.statement: _project_backdrop composites the field's own [[layers]] with `out = Image.alpha_composite(out.resize(im.size), im)`. It rescales the whole accumulated image to each later layer's pixel size, pastes that layer at (0,0), and ignores the `position`, `size`, `camera` and `shader` keys that build_overlays (build.py:5478-5491) honours. The `camera` argument is never used. One positioned crop therefore becomes the whole backdrop, stretched by the canvas over the camera frame. On a multi-camera field, the later camera's art paints over the picked camera's. `import --editable` writes exactly this shape: every depth group is a tight crop with explicit position/size (extract.py:1568). show_field routes any field with [[layers]] to this project surface (placedoc.py:553). The raycast still uses the correct camera and mesh, so written coordinates are right relative to the mesh, but the art the author clicks on does not match the room, which defeats 'click what you SEE'. A single full-cover layer (the new/floorplan/trace scaffolds) renders correctly.
findings.evidence: My probe v-place-bugs/p3_backdrop.py (real FieldProject.load + _project_backdrop) uses a 384x448 red cam-0 back layer, a 384x448 blue cam-1 layer and a 32x48 green crop at position [200,300]. Output: 'size: (32, 48) pixel(0,0): (40, 200, 40, 255)', meaning the whole backdrop is the crop. With only the two full-frame layers and camera 0, pixel(10,10) is blue (camera 1's art). I also checked that extract._render_depth_groups emits position/size per layer.
findings.user_path: ff9mapkit import <field> --editable -> open it -> Place -> Load the room.
findings.fix: Filter layers by int(layer.get('camera',0)) == the requested camera index. Composite onto a canvas the size of the camera range (times the layer upscale), pasting each layer resized to its `size` at its `position` (default: full cover), and never resize the accumulator. Treat additive (Abr) shaders as additive or skip them. Key the output per camera (see P9).

findings.title: Project surfaces are cached for the session; a changed walkmesh/camera never reaches Place, even on Load
findings.statement: PlaceDoc._bundles[(source, cam)] is filled once and never invalidated. show_field applies a cached bundle automatically (line 569), and on_load returns the cached bundle whenever the key exists (line 590), so 'Load the room' cannot refresh it. For a ('project', path) source, the camera, walkmesh and art can change mid-session: Trace regenerate, Floorplan recompose, a Blender re-export, or a hand edit of walkmesh.obj. Place keeps showing the old art and raycasting the old mesh, so drops land on coordinates resolved against geometry the build no longer ships. Only an app restart clears the cache. In addition, build_surface_from_project reads the toml from disk, so unsaved in-memory [camera]/[walkmesh] edits never show. Real-donor bundles are correctly static.
findings.evidence: Code read at placedoc.py 569-606. I re-ran place-code/p4_widget.py: after halving walkmesh.obj on disk and clicking Load again, it prints 'same bundle object? True x-extent -1200 1200', while 'a fresh build would give x-extent -600 600'.
findings.user_path: Load a traced/composed room in Place -> regenerate it in Trace or recompose in Floorplan (same path) -> return to Place / click Load: the old floor is still used.
findings.fix: For ('project', *) sources, validate the cached bundle against the mtimes of the toml, the walkmesh source and the layer images (store them in the bundle), or simply always rebuild a project surface on an explicit Load click and drop project bundles in show_field when the member/path changes. Keep the real-donor cache as it is. Separately, consider warning when the doc is dirty in [camera]/[walkmesh].

findings.title: Same member name, different file: the previous room's surface stays armed and clicks write into the new doc
findings.statement: show_field decides `same = member == self._member` by the [field] name alone. The canvas reset (gen bump, set_backdrop/surface/regions None, disarm) runs only when not same. The shell never calls place_doc.show_none when a project is opened. So when a different project with a same-named member is opened (composed rooms named A/B, or a re-scaffolded field), Place keeps the previous room's art, camera and walkmesh armed in place mode even though _bundle() for the new source is None. A click is raycast against the old room and written into the new doc. When the same member becomes blocked (protected), the stale surface also stays armed, but _on_surface_clicked refuses the write in that case.
findings.evidence: Code read at placedoc.py 532-574, and grep showing that shell.py never calls place_doc.show_none. I re-ran place-code/p5_state.py part 2: after show_field('FORK', data2, 'C:/other/FORK.field.toml'), 'bundle False | canvas place_mode True | surface tris 4', and a real QTest click writes an NPC at [3,1501] into data2. Part 4 shows the blocked case: 'same member now blocked: True | canvas place_mode still: True'.
findings.user_path: Open project 1, room 'A', Load in Place -> open project 2 which also has a room 'A' -> Place tab -> click the (old) art.
findings.fix: Compute `same` from (member, resolved path, source), not the name. In the else branch (no bundle or blocked), call self._apply_tool() (which disarms when not loaded) or explicitly disarm and clear the canvas.

findings.title: Placed markers cannot be dragged, renamed or deleted on the canvas; clicking one places another
findings.statement: Place-mode content markers (NPC/prop/chest/spawn/arrival) are inert. _draw_markers tags the anchor only data(0)='marker' with no index, no tooltip and no grabbable flag. mousePressEvent has branches for trace vertices, cut-outs and region handles but none for markers. contextMenuEvent falls through to super() outside region and trace mode. So a left-click on an existing marker is an ordinary slop-click: it raycasts and emits surface_clicked, and _apply_hit appends a SECOND NPC/prop at that spot. The only ways to fix a misplaced item are Undo (latest step only) or typing world coordinates in the Editor form, and the post-drop status names neither. The Regions tool on the same canvas has drag, rotate, retarget and delete, so the two tools are inconsistent. PLAN.md's Rung 3 record does not list marker editing as deferred.
findings.evidence: backdrop.py:416-439 (marker anchor has no index, tooltip or mark_grabbable), 1108-1148 (no marker branch on press), 1189-1197 (place mode always emits surface_clicked), 1210-1232 (no marker context menu). placedoc.py:843-861 appends on every surface click. studies/click-authoring/PLAN.md 786-807 does not mention moving or deleting markers.
findings.user_path: Place tab, Load the room, NPC mode: click the floor, then click the new marker to try to grab it. A second NPC appears on top.
findings.fix: Add the row index to content_markers. In _draw_markers tag the anchor (kind, index), give it a tooltip and mark_grabbable. In place mode, resolve 'marker' before raycasting on press: a drag re-raycasts and emits one marker_moved, the doc runs one pure move op plus one on_edit. A right-click menu offers Delete and Open in Editor. Copy the region drag and menu plumbing.

findings.title: Place's single non-wrapping control row floors the window past 1280 px at 150% and crushes controls at 1024@125%
findings.statement: The Place control row is one QHBoxLayout: an unelided field_label, Load, the camera combo, ToolStrip, four mode radios (plus the entrance spinner on Arrival), or the Regions cluster. Its sum sets the page minimum, and that sets the whole window floor. With a fork open, the window minimum width is 1117/1273/1391 px at 100/125/150% (place-regions 986/1128/1236). At 150% in the default 1280 window, the label loses its field number ('PLACEDEMO — donor') and the Inspector column is clipped ('PLAC', 'IDENTI'). At 1024 wide and 125%, the Load button reads 'ɔad the rooı' and both ToolStrip segments render as '…', so the author cannot tell Place from Regions. This is the same trap SpillRow (widgets.py:557) was built to cure on the Cutscene bar. The only fence (test_workspace_place.py:340) measures the fresh no-field state.
findings.evidence: Re-ran theme-scale-a11y-fences/probe_place.py (gui_snap on the native platform, WA_DontShowOnScreen) from my scratch dir. Output: '150 place-fork win minHint 1391 place_doc minHint 1121', field_label w 209 minHint 306, ToolStrip w 209 minHint 220; '125 place-fork win minHint 1273'; '100 place-fork win minHint 1117'. Read dracula-125-w1024/place-fork_dracula_125.png ('ɔad the rooı', '…' '…', 'PLACEDEMO —', Inspector cut) and mist-150/place-fork_mist_150.png (label cut after 'donor', Inspector 'PLAC').
findings.user_path: Set the text size to 150% in a 1280-wide window (or 125% at 1024), open a fork, go to Author > Place.
findings.fix: Make field_label a widgets.ElideLabel(min_ch≈10) with the full text in its tooltip. Wrap the row in widgets.SpillRow: lead = label + Load + camera, tail = ToolStrip + the active cluster. Add a fence on place_doc.minimumSizeHint with a fork fed, in both the place and regions tools. Re-snap at mist-150 and dracula-125-w1024.

findings.title: On-art labels, handles and the walkmesh footprint use UI palette tokens with no halo, and vanish on the art
findings.statement: Every BackdropCanvas overlay is a bare QGraphicsSimpleTextItem or shape in a palette token picked for the UI surface, painted straight onto arbitrary user art: horizon label :390, marker ring and label :419-439, cut-out diamond and label :475-490, region stroke and label :556/:650, pending and handle indices :681/:709, the walkmesh footprint :400. Against the fixture's tan floor (#9e8460), the ground content is authored on, the contrast is: accent 1.29 light / 1.11 dark / 1.83 mist / 1.47 dracula; warn 1.32 / 1.67 / 1.67 / 3.17; error 1.53 / 1.28 / 1.28 / 1.13. In light theme $text on the navy wall art is 1.15. So the cut-out label 'fg0 · z 1073' in light, the blue gateway labels in dark, and the red 'bad' states are close to unreadable. The footprint edge (accent at alpha 130) is weaker still on the floor. Pick any single token and some art defeats it, because hand-painted backgrounds span every luminance.
findings.evidence: Recomputed WCAG ratios from editor.theme.pick_palette for all four themes against #9e8460 and #26293a. Results match the reporters' numbers, e.g. light accent 1.29, dark accent 1.11, light text on navy 1.15. Read light-100/trace-contacts-canvas_light_100.png: the amber 'fg0 · z 1073' is barely visible on the tan floor. Read light-100/place-regions-canvas_light_100.png: amber labels and indices on tan or navy are hard to read, and the blue 'door0' is hard to read on navy.
findings.user_path: Any theme: draw regions, cut-outs or markers over the floor in Trace or Place.
findings.fix: Add one backdrop helper for on-art text: a translucent surface-coloured plate (the hint pill's rgba surface, about 0.85) behind each label, or a 2 px inverse-luminance outline via QPainterPathStroker. Give handles and glyphs a 1 px contrasting ring. Draw the footprint and outset edges as a dark underlay plus a light line. Apply it at all seven label call sites and fence it with a pixel-contrast check on the trace-contacts and place-regions snaps.

findings.title: Regenerate wipes hand [field] keys (location, title, text_block, borrow_bg)
findings.statement: merge_project_toml regenerates [field] wholesale, and the only report is 'retaken: field'. The Editor's own FIELD_SPEC form (editor/forms.py:77-88) writes text_block, title, location (the in-game LOCATION card) and borrow_bg into [field]. build.py also reads hide_area_title and other keys from that table. One Trace Regenerate erases all of them and does not name what was lost. The existing regression test does not catch this. test_imagefield._hand_author inserts text_block as a TOP-LEVEL bare key ('a bare key must precede [field]'), but build.py:363 reads [field].text_block, so the test covers a placement the Editor never writes.
findings.evidence: My probe p_t2.py set [field].location='Mog's Hut' and title through FieldDoc (the Editor's model), saved, then regenerated. 'before: {... 'location': "Mog's Hut", 'title': 'my notes'}', then 'after: {'id': 30500, 'name': 'M', 'area': 11} | retaken ['field'] kept []'. The reporter's text_block probe reproduced the same way.
findings.user_path: Generate a traced field, set Location in the Editor's Field form and save, then Regenerate from Trace. The location card is gone.
findings.fix: Merge [field] per key, as [player] is merged. The generator owns id, name and area; every other key rides through and is listed in kept. Name each overwritten generator key in retaken. Fix the test fixture so it puts text_block under [field].

findings.title: Trace: the unwrapped status line clips its key warnings, floors the window, and the canvas is starved to ~100-160 px at 125-150%
findings.statement: Six fixed rows stack above and below the Trace canvas: a two-line nameplate, the photo/pitch row, the tools row, the cut-out strip once a contact exists, the Name/Id/Generate row and the status line. self.status is a QLabel without word wrap. _refresh APPENDS its warnings after the counts: door-without-target, law warnings, above-horizon counts, and last of all '⚠ not stamped — Regenerate X to update the project'. The pitch-drift warning also lands at the end. So the most important clause is the one cut off the right edge, and the unwrapped label makes its full text width the page minimum. Measured on the native platform in a 1280x850 window, with the window minimum in brackets: contacts state canvas 320 px at 100% (998), 230 px at 125% (1198), 158 px at 150% (1348, wider than the window, so the Inspector clips). At 100%, with a project generated and one untargeted door, the status needs 1099 px of 984 and the visible text ends 'Regenerate PICTURE to '.
findings.evidence: Re-ran probe_place.py natively: '150 trace-contacts win minHint 1348 trace_doc minHint 1078 canvas h 158', '125 ... 1198 ... canvas h 230', '100 ... 998 ... canvas h 320'. The reporter's probe3.out (valid: it drives load_image, a Generate, then a real region draw): 'status label width 984 text needs 1099 -> clipped True'. Code: tracedoc.py:266-268 (no setWordWrap), 412-414 (not-stamped appended last); placedoc.py:506 wraps its status.
findings.user_path: Trace a photo, Generate, then edit anything; or use text size 125-150%, or a 1024-wide window.
findings.fix: self.status.setWordWrap(True), capped at two lines (Place's idiom), and put the warn clauses (not stamped, pitch drift, untargeted doors) FIRST. Set the full text as the tooltip. To win canvas height back, merge the cut-out strip into the tools row as the Cut-outs tool's own cluster, and make the nameplate prose one line. Fence trace_doc.minimumSizeHint in the contacts state.

findings.title: An un-generated trace has no unsaved-work guard: closing the app or opening another image discards it silently
findings.statement: A Trace session (floor, cut-out anchors and offsets, gateway and event quads with their targets and per-zone messages) exists only in memory until Generate writes the .trace.json sidecar. closeEvent calls _maybe_prompt_unsaved, which looks only at _dirty_members() (field documents). It has no term for trace_doc, so the window closes without a prompt. Inside the tab, on_open, the 'Load <open field>' offer, load_trace and load_project all go through load_image, which clears floor, fg, regions AND _history with no confirmation, so Undo cannot recover the session. Event messages exist only in the session, by design (ev_msg tooltip). TraceDoc already tracks the needed state (_stamped=False after any gesture), but nothing reads it. Losing a long tracing session is real data loss of the author's work.
findings.evidence: My probe /v-trace-tab/p_doc.py: mid-session 'floor 4 regions 1 hist 4' > on_open(another photo) > 'floor 0 regions 0 hist 0 undo False'. I read shell.py:7643-7660 and 7715-7721: there is no trace_doc reference in the close path, and the grep of trace_doc in shell.py shows only construction, retheme/scale, the rail and the tab-show offer. Note: shell-lifecycle probe3's 'closeEvent accepted' line is vacuous evidence, because _maybe_prompt_unsaved returns True unconditionally under QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen. The code read is what decides this.
findings.user_path: Trace tab > trace a floor, draw doors and type event messages > close the app (or Open another image) > everything is gone with no prompt.
findings.fix: Add TraceDoc.has_unsaved() (an image is loaded, the trace or regions are not empty, and either no project is set up or not _stamped). Fold it into _maybe_prompt_unsaved ('Discard the traced session?') and check it in on_open and on_offer before load_*. Better still, autosave the session to a per-user scratch .trace.json.

findings.title: Ctrl+Z on the Trace tab undoes an unrelated field edit and jumps to another tab; the trace is untouched
findings.statement: The window-level Ctrl+Z QShortcut (shell.py:1595) calls _undo_shortcut. That function only hands off to a focused text widget, otherwise it pops the shell's _undo_stack of committed field edits. TraceDoc's history can be reached only through its own Undo button, and BackdropCanvas.keyPressEvent does not handle Ctrl+Z. So a real Ctrl+Z pressed on the Trace canvas leaves the trace gesture in place. If a field is open (always true after a first Generate, which opens the traced project), it reverts that field's last edit, and _apply_history moves the author to the tab that edit belongs to. Redo can recover it, but the author has unknowingly undone real work in another surface. The doc-local undo itself is by design (PLAN.md:388); routing the key to it is not covered by any design note or test.
findings.evidence: My probe /v-trace-tab/p_ctrlz.py sends a REAL Ctrl+Z key event (QTest.keyClick through the shortcut map, focus on BackdropCanvas) with a Cutscene '+ Scene' edit on the shell undo stack. Result: 'after real Ctrl+Z: tab = Cutscene | trace floor 3 | shell undo stack: [] | redo: ['add cutscene scene']'. The trace was not changed, the cutscene edit was undone, and the tab switched. Grep shows no Ctrl+Z test or QShortcut in tracedoc, floorplandoc or backdrop.
findings.user_path: Open a field, make any Cutscene, Place or form edit > go to Trace > click a wrong vertex > press Ctrl+Z.
findings.fix: In _undo_shortcut and _redo_shortcut, when the current tab has a doc-local history (trace_doc.on_undo; the same for floorplan), send the key there and return. Keep the toolbar Undo app-level, but name its scope in the tooltip on those tabs.

findings.title: A say step with signal = "+" or true cannot be applied from the editor
findings.statement: The build accepts signal as "+" (increment, [INCS]), true or an int (build.py:2996-3000), and its own wait_signal lint tells authors to 'Add signal = "+"' to their lines. read_step converts signal with int(), so opening such a step and pressing Apply fails with 'signal must be a whole number'. This happens even with no change, or with only the text edited, so the recommended form locks the step out of the editor. True is displayed as the text 'True'. The field label 'Signal when typed (n or blank)' never mentions '+'.
findings.evidence: p1_roundtrip.py, cases 1 and 2: note "signal must be a whole number (got '+')" and "(got 'True')", and the step is left unchanged. grep in build.py: line 8979 is the lint text recommending signal = "+".
findings.user_path: A say line carrying signal = "+" (which the build's own lint suggests): open it in the editor and press Apply.
findings.fix: Parse signal as follows: '+' stays '+', digits become an int, a blank clears it, anything else is an error. Show True as '+'. Update the label and tooltip to 'n, + or blank'.

findings.title: PROBLEMS says 'No structural problems' for conductor errors the tab's own gestures create
findings.statement: scene_problems covers only part of build._validate_conductor. It misses five rules. (a) A with_prev group whose leader is not walk, path, animation or turn; moving a say above a with_prev turn with the arrow buttons creates this. (b) The same actor twice in one parallel group; duplicating a with_prev turn creates this. (c) An untagged actor step in a cast of two or more, even though the actor field's placeholder says 'blank = sole cast member'. (d) A scene with an empty steps list, which deleting every row produces. (e) Invalid tail codes and style names. In each case the tab shows 'No structural problems.' while the build and the Workspace Check refuse the field. The docstring does call the lane 'cheap raw-only structural checks', so incompleteness is acknowledged, but (a), (b) and (d) are structural and are produced by the tab's own buttons. Severity is downgraded from major: the build catches every case before deploy, so the cost is a misleading readout and a late surprise, not bad bytes.
findings.evidence: Re-ran p5_problems_parity.py and p5b.py, which compare scene_problems with build.validate: TAB [] against BUILD errors for all six cases, for example "step 1 has a with_prev beat after it but isn't a walk/path/animation/turn" and "actor 'Mira' already acts in this parallel group". Code read: _sync_with_prev checks only the step's own kind and row.
findings.user_path: Cutscene ladder: move a say above a with_prev turn, or duplicate a with_prev turn, or delete every step. The PROBLEMS panel stays clean.
findings.fix: Add to scene_problems: a pass over conductor.group_parallel (leader kind plus per-group actor uniqueness), the missing-actor rule for multi-actor casts, empty steps, and TAIL_CODES/resolve_style checks. Fence each rule against build.validate the way dispatch_problems is fenced.

findings.title: PROBLEMS flags actor = "player" outside the cast, which the build and compiler accept
findings.statement: scene_problems reports an error for any step actor not listed in the scene's cast. build._validate_conductor deliberately uses known = set(cast) | {'player'}, and the compiler supports it: _gen_conductor_step_tags puts a player step's tag on the player's own entry (uid 250) whether or not 'player' is in actors. The tab therefore shows a red error that the build does not raise. The tab's rule is the wrong one, and no fence ties the two together.
findings.evidence: p5b.py: TAB ['scene #0: step 1 actor "player" is not in the cast (Cid, Mira)'] / BUILD []. Read build.py:9005 (known includes player) and build.py:6908-6928, where _tag_target('player') resolves to the player entry independently of the cast.
findings.user_path: A cast scene with actors = ["Cid"] and a step { walk = ..., actor = "player" }.
findings.fix: Treat 'player' as known in scene_problems. Also consider whether stage_model and stage_verdicts should stage a player who acts outside the cast, since they currently iterate cast members only. Add a parity fence.

findings.title: Duplicate Scene copies a pinned once-flag, so the two scenes share one once-bit
findings.statement: duplicate_scene deep-copies the whole block, including an explicit flag (the advanced 'Once-flag override'). After the author changes the duplicate's gate, as the button's tooltip tells them to, both scenes test and set the same gEventGlobal once-bit. Whichever plays first marks the bit, and the other one silently never plays. Neither the tab's PROBLEMS lane nor build.validate reports a shared once-flag. This only bites when the source scene has an explicit flag, which is an advanced field mainly used for a campaign member's 2nd+ scene. That makes it an edge case, so severity is downgraded from major.
findings.evidence: Re-ran p9_dupflag.py: 'shared once-flag: 8712 8712', 'TAB: []', 'BUILD: []'. Code read: duplicate_scene is a bare copy.deepcopy(cur[k]). build.py:3493/7945 read cs['flag'] per block with no uniqueness check.
findings.user_path: A scene with Once-flag override set, then the Scene duplicate button, then a new gate on the copy, then build and play. The second scene never fires.
findings.fix: In duplicate_scene, drop 'flag' from the copy (the build then auto-allocates for a single field; for a campaign member it refuses loudly, which is the right prompt) and say so in the edit label. Add a pairwise-distinct once-flag rule to dispatch_problems and build.validate.

findings.title: Unapplied Scene-settings edits are silently wiped by any re-render
findings.statement: With the Scene settings card open, CutsceneDoc._render() calls _fill_settings() every time, and that tears the form down and rebuilds it from the document. Anything typed but not yet applied is lost. Many things trigger _render: every tab show (shell.py:4991 re-feeds show_field for the same member), a tree selection while the tab is current (shell.py:4867), any committed edit (a stage-handle drag goes through _after_edit, and the shell's _on_cutscene_edit re-feeds again), undo, and a retheme. The step editor survives the same re-feed because _sync_insets only re-seats it. So the two accordion panels in one tab behave differently, and the settings card has no dirty marker to warn the author. Plain step selection (_on_step_select) does not re-render, so it keeps the typed values.
findings.evidence: Re-ran cutscene-code/p6_settings_loss.py: typed 150 into the gate, which survived a step select (150), then a stage drag of the selected walk target gave 'after a stage drag: 100 settings open: True', with the doc still at 100. Re-ran cutscene-ux-look/probe_flows.py natively (WA_DontShowOnScreen): '1. typed gate before refeed: 777' then 'gate field after same-field refeed: 100'. Both probes drive real user paths: show_field on the same member is exactly what the shell's tab-show hook calls (shell.py:4991, _feed_cutscene at :5073). No doc or test records this as intended.
findings.user_path: Cutscene tab > Settings > type a new 'Requires beat' > click the Editor tab to look up an NPC name > come back to Cutscene: the typed value is gone. Or: type a gate, then drag the selected walk's target on the stage.
findings.fix: Record the (member, scene, block snapshot) the form was built from, and in _render skip _fill_settings when it is unchanged, so a same-field re-feed re-seats the existing form. Rebuild only on a scene/field change, or when the block really changed (undo/Apply). Optionally show an 'unapplied changes' marker on Apply.

findings.title: Half-typed step-editor text discarded by rowtools, scene switch, Edit on another row
findings.statement: _move_step, _dup_step, _del_step, _on_scene_select and _del_scene all call _close_editor(), which only hides the editor and clears its target. _edit_step on a different row calls open_step(), which overwrites the widgets. None of these checks whether the editor holds edits that were never applied. A user part-way through a long say line who clicks ↑/↓/⧉/✕ on any row, clicks another scene, or opens another row's pencil loses the line with no warning. Closing the editor on a structural edit is deliberate (the comment notes that indices shift), but losing the typed text is not discussed anywhere.
findings.evidence: Re-ran cutscene-code/p11_editor_misc.py: _edit_step(2), typed text into value_text, then _move_step(0,+1) gave 'editor open after ↓ on another row: False | typed text survives in doc: False'. Read the code at lines 1067, 1133, 1198-1206 and 1273-1290: no dirty check anywhere.
findings.user_path: Open a step's pencil, type a new line, then click ↓ on a neighbouring row (or select another scene): the text is gone.
findings.fix: Keep the step the editor was opened on, and treat read_step() != that step as dirty. When dirty, either auto-apply before the structural edit (simplest and consistent with the Apply-advances flow) or refuse the edit with a note in the editor. Add mode is dirty whenever value_text or value_line is non-empty.

findings.title: The storyboard keeps the previous beat on screen after the scene loses all its steps
findings.statement: When storyboard() returns no beats and no error (every step deleted), _refresh_board disables the slider and calls _show_beat, which returns early on an empty beats list. board_say, board_pos and the ladder beat marks keep the old values, and canvas.set_storyboard is never called. The canvas therefore keeps drawing the old board's beat positions and labels over a scene that has no steps.
findings.evidence: Re-ran p7_board_stale.py, which uses the public _del_step (the delete button) three times with the board on: 'beat 1 of 1 | say: Cid: Made it to the altar. | canvas beatpos items: 2 | slider enabled False', 'canvas board beats: 1 doc board beats: 0'.
findings.user_path: Turn the storyboard on, then delete every step of the scene with the delete button.
findings.fix: In _refresh_board, when beats is empty: set board_say to a 'no steps yet' message, clear board_pos, call ladder.set_beat_marks(()) and call canvas.set_storyboard(None).

findings.title: Storyboard say strip shows 'Name:' attribution the game never renders
findings.statement: _show_beat writes f"{say_actor}:\n" followed by the wrapped bare line. say_actor is speaker OR actor (cutscenescan.py:450). The compiler attributes a cutscene line only through `speaker`, via text.with_speaker (build.py:6613): the name, a newline, then the line in curly quotes, with no colon. An actor-only say gets no name in game. So the strip shows a colon form the game does not use, shows a name for actor-only lines that the game leaves unattributed, and wraps the unquoted line. The added quotes can move a line break near the width limit. The ▶ Storyboard tooltip promises 'the say line shows with its final in-game wrapping'. test_cutscenedoc.py:272 asserts 'Cid:' is in the strip, so that test needs updating with any fix. It pins the presence of an attribution, not a design decision about the colon.
findings.evidence:
Re-ran cutscene-code/p12_wrap.py: BOARD 'Cid:
We made it to the altar at last, all of
us.' vs GAME 'Cid
“We made it…
us.”'; BOARD 'Mira:
Quiet now.' vs GAME 'Quiet now.'. Confirmed the compile path: build.py:6613 `line = _text.with_speaker(s.get("speaker"), _cutscene.step_text(s))`. Actor is not consulted there.
findings.user_path: Storyboard on a scene whose say step has speaker = 'Cid', or only actor = 'Mira'.
findings.fix: Build the strip text as the build does: _dlg.wrap_preview(_text.with_speaker(s.get('speaker'), line), ww). That needs the beat to carry `speaker` separately from `actor` (cutscenescan.storyboard sets say_who = speaker or actor). Show actor-only attribution, if at all, as a muted caption such as '(bubble on Mira)'. Update test_cutscenedoc.py:272.

findings.title: The stage canvas is starved by the fixed ladder split (storyboard on, 150%, 1024 wide); dead space under short ladders at 100%
findings.statement: The vertical ladder/stage split is set once to [340k, 280k] at build time. Nothing re-balances it for content, the storyboard strip or CALIBRE: _toggle_board only shows the bar, set_scale only changes the board slider's minimum, and _ladder_guard's 140px canvas floor runs only when an editor or settings panel opens. Results: at 100% with a 3-step scene, about 35% of the ladder pane is empty while the stage is a modest strip. With the storyboard on at 150% in the default 1280x850 window, or at 125% in 1024x720, the stage is a strip of roughly 60-150 logical px. There the 'Ctrl+scroll zooms · Ctrl+0 fits' hint sits on top of the routed leg and the 'Cid' label, and the leg runs off the bottom edge. The inspector clipping that report #9 also mentions is the same defect as C31.
findings.evidence: Read the PNGs. mist-150/cutscene-storyboard_mist_150.png: the stage occupies display y≈1010-1180 of 1328, the hint pill overlaps the walk leg and 'Cid', and the leg exits the bottom. mist-100/cutscene-doc-pane: ladder rows end at about y640 of a pane that runs to about y970. dracula-125-w1024 staged/editor: the stage is a short strip. Code: line 888 setSizes; _toggle_board (1368) and set_scale (949) never touch _vsplit; _ladder_guard (1222) is only called from _edit_step/_add_step.
findings.user_path: Open Cutscene at 150% text (or a 1024-wide window) and press ▶ Storyboard: the stage, which is the storyboard's subject, is a sliver.
findings.fix: Size the ladder pane to min(content height, ~50%) on render while the user has not dragged the splitter (track splitterMoved). Give the canvas a scaled floor, about 200*scale/100, that _toggle_board also enforces. Refit the canvas after the split changes. Hide the zoom hint when the canvas is under a minimum height.

findings.title: Opening the step editor scrolls its header and the edited row out of view
findings.statement: _reveal_editor calls ensureWidgetVisible(self.editor, 0, 40). The editor (about 610px) is about twice the ladder viewport's height (about 300px at default sizes), and Qt centres a too-tall widget, so the editor's top lands above the viewport. At 100% the header band is clipped by a few pixels: Apply and Close are still readable, but the row being edited and every ladder row above it are scrolled away, which defeats the accordion's purpose ('the conversation stays visible around the line'). At 125% in a 1024 window the header, Apply and Close are entirely off-screen and the Type combo is sliced in half. The add lane calls _reveal_editor after every Apply, so this repeats on each typed line. Severity is minor rather than the reported major: at the default 100% the controls remain reachable.
findings.evidence: Re-ran cutscene-ux-look/probe_flows.py natively: '2. viewport h 298 editor h 610 apply_btn y in viewport -8 scroll 163'. Read mist-100/cutscene-editor-pane (header clipped about 8px, no ladder rows visible) and dracula-125-w1024/cutscene-editor-pane (no header, 'Say (dialogue)' combo cut in half). The docsite figure editor-cutscene_light.png shows the same.
findings.user_path: Click a row's pencil (or ＋ Step and Apply lines in the add lane).
findings.fix: Scroll so the editor's TOP plus one row above it is visible, e.g. self._lscroll.verticalScrollBar().setValue(max(0, self.editor.y() - row_h - 8)) after the layout settles. Do not centre a panel taller than the viewport.

findings.title: 'Beat' means both a story ScenarioCounter value and a storyboard step group
findings.statement: In the rail and scene header ('plays at beat 100', cutscenescan.gate_text) and in Settings ('Requires beat', 'Then set beat', forms.py:262/270), 'beat' means the story ScenarioCounter value. In the storyboard ('beat 1 of 2', 'beats, not seconds') and the step editor ('Runs with the previous beat'), a beat is a group of steps that run together. Both meanings appear together on screen in storyboard mode, and the S5 tutorial (lines 80-82) uses both in one sentence. The premise is true and a string-only rename is worth doing. Severity is minor, not major: nothing is mis-built, it is vocabulary confusion.
findings.evidence: Read the mist-150 storyboard snap: 'plays at beat 100' in the scene header and 'beat 1 of 2' in the strip are visible together. Grepped forms.py:262-271, cutscenescan.py:161, cutscenedoc.py:312/1425, and s5-cutscene-and-music.md:80-82. Tests pin the strings (test_cutscenedoc.py:200 'plays at beat 100', :271 'beat 2 of 2'), but as regression strings, not as a recorded naming decision.
findings.user_path: Open a gated scene and press ▶ Storyboard.
findings.fix: Keep 'story beat' (or 'story point') for the ScenarioCounter gate, e.g. 'plays at story beat 100' and 'Requires story beat', and rename the storyboard unit ('moment 1 of 2', 'Runs together with the previous step'). Update the strings in cutscenescan.gate_text, CUTSCENE_SPEC, StepEditor.with_prev, _show_beat, the two tests and the S5 doc.

findings.title: Scene rail rows clip mid-glyph behind a permanent horizontal scrollbar
findings.statement: Each rail item is 'scene #k · plays at beat N · cast n · m steps' in a plain QListWidget with the default as-needed horizontal scrollbar. Because the list scrolls horizontally, QListWidget's default ElideRight never applies, and the text is cut mid-character ('beat 10(' at 100%, 'plays a' at 150%, 'plays' at 125%/1024), above a horizontal scrollbar. The cast/narration kind and the step count, the parts that tell scenes apart, are never visible without scrolling. The code comment at line 893 says the 200px budget was chosen so the gate would fit, and it does not fit.
findings.evidence: Read mist-100/cutscene-doc-pane ('scene #0 · plays at beat 10(' plus a horizontal scrollbar), mist-150/cutscene-storyboard ('plays a') and dracula-125-w1024/cutscene-staged ('plays'). Code: lines 731-737 (no scrollbar or elide policy) and 1026-1030.
findings.user_path: Any field with a cutscene, on the Cutscene tab.
findings.fix: self.rail.setHorizontalScrollBarPolicy(ScrollBarAlwaysOff) so the default ElideRight works (the tooltip already has the full text), and reorder the text to put the distinguishing parts first ('scene #0 · 3 steps · cast 2 · beat 100'). Two-line items are optional.

findings.title: Staging problems list truncates the build's sentence and is not clickable
findings.statement: stage_list is a QListWidget with no word wrap, inside the narrow docked inspector. The build's staging sentence ('⚠ [cutscene] #0 step 0: walk target … is off the walkmesh …') shows as a stub: 'walk ta' at 100%, and only '⚠ |' at 125%/1024. REVIEW.md accepts off-view canvas verdicts as a known-small on the grounds that 'the note + list carry the words', but the list does not show the words, so the mitigation fails. No itemClicked or activated handler is connected, so a row cannot take the author to the failing step or the verdict spot.
findings.evidence: Code lines 928-931: no setWordWrap, no signal connection. Grepped for stage_list connections: none. Read dracula-125-w1024/cutscene-staged_dracula_125.png: the list shows only '⚠ |' with a scrollbar. REVIEW.md:41-42 records the 'note + list carry the words' rationale.
findings.user_path: Press Check the staging on a scene with a stalled walk.
findings.fix: setWordWrap(True) plus ScrollBarAlwaysOff on the list (or word-wrapped captions instead). On itemClicked, select the scene/step and centre the canvas on the verdict's b-point. Optionally strip the '[cutscene] #k' prefix when the scene is already selected.

findings.title: Stage labels collide with markers; storyboard toggle does not refit the canvas
findings.statement: _decollide_labels only avoids other labels. Its down-tier guard clears only the label's own marker row, never other markers or legs, and no leader line is drawn when a label moves. At 125% and 150% the 'player spawn' label is pushed down a tier onto Cid's start dot and the walk leg (the dot sits inside the word), and 'Cid' jams against Tam's dot. Separately, _toggle_board shows the storyboard bar, which takes height from the canvas, without refitting, so edge markers (Mira) can be clipped at the bottom until the user presses Ctrl+0.
findings.evidence: Read behaviordoc.py:260-300: the overlap test only compares against `placed` label rects. Read dracula-125-w1024/cutscene-staged and editor-pane: 'player spawn' is drawn across Cid's filled dot and the leg, and 'Cid' touches Tam's dot. mist-150 storyboard: 'player spawn' crosses the cyan marker. _toggle_board (cutscenedoc.py:1368) has no fit call.
findings.user_path: Cutscene tab at 125%/150%, or toggling ▶ Storyboard.
findings.fix: Add marker rects (radius plus a margin) to `placed` before placing labels, and draw a 1px leader when a label moves more than one tier. Call canvas fit (when the user has not zoomed) after _toggle_board and after any split change.

findings.title: Step selection is nearly invisible and mouse-only, yet it drives insert position and drag handles
findings.statement: Selecting a ladder row only changes its index chip from 'n' to '▸ n'. The _StepRow frame gets no property and no QSS. In storyboard mode the beat marks override the chip with '▶ n', a near-identical glyph, so the selection disappears. Clicking a selected row again silently deselects it (line 1075). The selection decides where ＋ Step inserts, and it is the only way to get the stage's drag handle for a walk target, which the stage never hints at. _StepRow is a QFrame with NoFocus and no key handling, so selection needs the mouse.
findings.evidence: probe_flows.py (native): "5. row props: [('card', None, ''), ('card', None, '')] ['0', '▸ 1']": selection changes only the chip text. probe_kb.py: 'rows focusable: [_StepRow:0 ...]' (NoFocus). Code _chip_text (549-554) gives beat marks precedence over selection.
findings.user_path: Click a ladder row, then press ＋ Step or try to find the drag handle.
findings.fix: Set a 'selected' dynamic property on the selected _StepRow and add a QSS accent border/left-rail, matching the rail's selected idiom. Keep selection visible in storyboard mode (property-based, not the chip). Optionally make rows focusable with Up/Down and Enter.

findings.title: S5 tutorial ignores the seeded 'A new scene.' step; its figure hides the ladder and shows elided buttons
findings.statement: The tutorial says to press Add a scene, then 'Build a three-step narration: press ＋ Step…'. Add a scene mints {say = 'A new scene.'} (cutscenescan._SCENE_MINT, line 550), so following the steps gives four steps, with the placeholder line first, and it ships in-game unless the author notices it. The embedded figure (docsite/assets/shots/editor-cutscene_light.png, captioned 'the scene rail, the step ladder, and the step editor open') shows no ladder rows, because the editor is centred over them (C18). Its bar reads '+ St…' and 'Sce…' (C17) while the text says to press '＋ Step'.
findings.evidence: Read s5 lines 49-60 and cutscenescan.py:550. Read the figure PNG: header 'Step 2 — edit', no ladder rows, '+ St…', '⧉ Sce…', rail clipped.
findings.user_path: A newcomer following S5 step 1.
findings.fix: Tell the reader the new scene starts with one placeholder line and to rewrite it first (pencil on row 0), so the build is that line plus two more. Alternatively, have Add a scene open the editor on the seeded step. Re-take the figure after the C17/C18 fixes.

findings.title: Docked instruments column overflows the inspector: 'Chec', '⚠ 1 sta', '⚠ |'
findings.statement: The Cutscene instruments column (Problems/Staging) is wider than the inspector's viewport, and it clips at the right edge instead of wrapping. At 1024x720 and 125% the window grab (exactly 1024 wide, so this is not a snap artifact) shows 'PROBL', 'STAGIN', 'Chec', '⚠ 1 sta / across 1', a problems list of only '⚠ |', and 'Ope'. Even at the default 1280x850 window at 150% it reads 'Check the stagi', 'No structural proble' and 'Open the .tom'. Even the word-wrapped problems label clips, so the column's content width exceeds the viewport. The docstring's claim ('everything here wraps or scrolls internally') does not hold.
findings.evidence: Read dracula-125-w1024/cutscene-staged_dracula_125.png (3072px = 1024x3, grabbed via w.grab() in gui_snap) and mist-150/cutscene-storyboard_mist_150.png. Both show the right column truncated mid-word. Code _build_instruments (900-939): QPushButtons with fixed text, no elide, and a non-wrapping stage_list.
findings.user_path: Cutscene tab at 150% text, or in a 1024-wide window.
findings.fix: Make the column yield: use ElideButton (after the C17 fix) or wrapping for the two buttons, give stage_list word wrap with its horizontal scrollbar off, and make sure the inspector host gives the column the viewport width (setWidgetResizable plus a horizontal minimum the dock honours). Re-check the Behavior and Place instrument columns, which dock into the same host.

findings.title: The tab never explains how to see a gated or play-once scene in game
findings.statement: A scene with 'Requires beat'/'Requires flag' plays only when the save's story state matches, and a 'Play once' scene hides after its first viewing. Nothing in the tab says how to reach either state. The header just says 'plays at beat 100'. No string in cutscenedoc.py mentions the ~ debug menu, reloading or retesting. The minted scene is ungated, so the S5 happy path is not affected (S5 also explains a redeploy resets the once-flag), and tutorial 08:108 mentions '~ → Flags' for retesting. But an author who adds a gate gets no guidance in the tab, and 'deployed, walked in, nothing happened' is the likely result. A one-line caption is cheap and worth it. Caveat: before naming a lever in the caption, verify which debug-menu path can actually set the ScenarioCounter; that was not verified here.
findings.evidence: Grepped cutscenedoc.py for '~', 'Flags', 'Reload', 'debug': none. Read s5:66-71 (redeploy resets the once-flag) and 08-dialogue-cutscene.md:108 ('retest with ~ → Flags'). gate_text (cutscenescan.py:158-167) is the only gate surface.
findings.user_path: Set Requires beat = 100 on a scene, deploy, walk in on a save at a different story point.
findings.fix: When the selected scene is gated or once, show a muted caption under the scene bar naming how to reach it in game (the debug-menu lever that sets the story point or flag, then ~ → Reload field). Confirm the exact lever in game first.

findings.title: No facing indicator for turn steps; the cast is free text (but typos ARE flagged live)
findings.statement: The premise is partly true. A 'turn 128' step is a raw 0-255 facing byte with no stage representation: stage_model and the storyboard draw positions and legs only, so a turn beat changes nothing on the canvas. The Settings Cast is a plain STRLIST line edit with no catalog picker.
