The claim that a cast typo surfaces 'only after a staging run' is wrong: cutscenescan.scene_problems (lines 279-289), which runs in the always-on PROBLEMS lane on every render, flags 'cast member "X" is not an [[npc]] on this field' and 'step i actor "X" is not in the cast' immediately after Apply. A facing tick and a cast picker are reasonable improvements. A 'pick the turn on the stage' tool needs the camera-yaw/facing-byte frame (the laying-out skill's trap), so it is medium effort and needs an in-game check.
findings.evidence: Read cutscenescan.scene_problems (259-289): live unknown-cast and unknown-actor checks. CutsceneStage drawing (cutscenedoc.py:150-215): no facing glyph. CUTSCENE_SPEC 'actors' is STRLIST with no catalog (forms.py:260).
findings.user_path: Author a turn step; type a misspelled cast name in Settings.
findings.fix: Draw a short facing tick on cast markers (end-of-beat facing in storyboard mode) using the kit's facing-byte to world convention, and give Cast a catalog picker of [[npc]] names plus 'player' via the existing pick seam. A stage pick for turn angles comes later and needs a playtest to confirm the direction convention.

findings.title: A staging verdict can paint off-screen because a same-scene re-render never refits; the 'staged' snap shows no verdict label
findings.statement: _finish_stage calls canvas.set_verdicts(rows), which redraws without a refit, and same-scene re-renders keep the user's zoom by design (set_scene refit only on a field or scene switch). When an edit moves a walk target outside the previously fitted bounds, the stall label and ring paint outside the viewport and only part of the red line is visible; Ctrl+0 (which includes verdict points in _pts) recovers it. This is narrower than claimed. A typical stall, a target across a wall inside the field, lands within the existing fit and is visible, so only the off-field target case hides it. The snap point stands: the gui_snap 'staged' state uses walk [2000, 2000] through doc._render() with no refit, so the figure meant to show 'a staging verdict painted on the failing leg' shows no verdict label at all and cannot fail on its own subject.
findings.evidence: Read review-ctp/light-100/cutscene-staged-canvas_light_100.png: both scrollbars are present, a red line leaves the top edge from Cid, and there is no 'stalls here' label or verdict ring anywhere. Read gui_snap.py:2166-2170 (the 'staged' state mutates the steps, calls _render() and stage_now with no fit). Code path: set_verdicts -> _draw has no _fit.
findings.user_path: Edit a walk target to a coordinate far outside the stage's current extent, then press Check the staging: the Inspector reports a problem but the stage shows no marker until Ctrl+0.
findings.fix: In _finish_stage (or CutsceneStage.set_verdicts), if any verdict endpoint lies outside mapToScene(viewport().rect()), call ensureVisible on the first one (preferred over a full refit, so the user's zoom survives). Make the snap state press fit or assert that the label is inside the viewport.

findings.title: Keyboard reorder loses focus every time; ladder rows cannot take focus
findings.statement: StepLadder.set_rows deletes and rebuilds every row on each structural edit, so the focused ↑/↓/⧉/✕ button is destroyed. Focus falls to an unrelated, unnamed QToolButton outside the ladder, and a keyboard user must Tab back through the toolbar, rail and every earlier row's five tools to continue. _StepRow is NoFocus with no key handling, so a keyboard user cannot select a row, and selection decides where ＋ Step inserts. That leaves keyboard users able to insert only at the end, or after the row whose pencil they opened. Severity is minor rather than major: real, but it affects keyboard-only authoring of a mouse-centric canvas tool.
findings.evidence: Re-ran theme-scale-a11y-fences/probe_kb.py (native, hidden, gui_snap's _make_win with pinned prefs): 'focus before: True Move this step down — step 0', then after Space 'focus after: QToolButton  steps now: ['turn', 'walk', 'say']', and 'rows focusable: ['_StepRow:0', '_StepRow:0']'. The probe uses a real key press on the real button.
findings.user_path: Tab to a row's ↓ button and press Space.
findings.fix: After a move/dup/delete in _after_edit, restore focus to the tool with the same glyph on the step's new index (find it by accessibleName '… — step j'). Optionally make _StepRow TabFocus with Up/Down to select and Enter to edit.

findings.title: Settings card controls and the wrap preview have no accessible names (and so does every forms_qt form)
findings.statement: With the Scene settings card open, 7 QLineEdits and 1 QCheckBox expose no accessible name, and the step editor's read-only wrap-preview QPlainTextEdit is unnamed too. The cause is in the shared builder: forms_qt.build_form adds each field as QFormLayout.addRow(label, box), where `box` is a container widget, not the input, and the label is sometimes a QWidget wrapper (the concept-badge case). No buddy reaches the input and no accessibleName is set. So this is not Cutscene-specific: every form build_form produces (the Editor tab's NPC/chest/event/field/choice forms, battledoc, tuningdialog) has unnamed inputs. The house a11y fence walks tabs only in the no-field state and never meets a built form.
findings.evidence: Re-ran theme-scale-a11y-fences/probe_names.py: 'cutscene-settings unnamed: 7 QLineEdit + 1 QCheckBox', 'cutscene-editor unnamed: [QPlainTextEdit ro=True]'. My own probe (v-cutscene-ux/names.py) called build_form directly on every *_SPEC: 'CHEST_SPEC unnamed 10 of 10', 'EVENT_SPEC unnamed 12 of 12', 'FIELD_SPEC unnamed 7 of 7', 'CUTSCENE_SPEC unnamed 10 of 10'. build_form call sites: shell.py:7448/7803/7830, battledoc.py:491, tuningdialog.py:166, cutscenedoc.py:1160.
findings.user_path: Screen-reader user tabs through any Editor form or the Cutscene Scene settings card.
findings.fix: In build_form, call widget.setAccessibleName(f.label) on each field's input (and, when the label is a QLabel, label.setBuddy(widget)). That fixes every form at once. Name the wrap preview in _wrap_preview_panel ('In-game wrap preview'). Extend the a11y fence to build one spec's form and assert every input is named.

findings.title: Tab order leaves the Cutscene tab before reaching the step rows and the open editor; Apply and Close come before the fields
findings.statement: The ladder rows are rebuilt on every render, so their row tools and the inset step editor join the window's focus chain last. From the scene rail, Tab goes through the scene bar and the stage, then leaves the tab for the console toggle, the Beginner toggle, Deploy and the inspector's Check and Open .toml. Only after those does it reach the step rows' ↑ ↓ edit ⧉ ✕ and the editor. Inside the editor, Apply and Close come before Type, Dialogue and Actor. The read-only wrap-preview box is also a Tab stop. Nothing calls setTabOrder.
findings.evidence: Probe probes/x-cutscene-place/p6_keyboard.py walks Qt's TabFocus chain from the rail (output in p6.out): '8 CutsceneStage IN · 9 QScrollArea out · 10 consoleToggle out · 11 Beginner mode out · 12 Deploy out · 13 Check the staging out · 14 Open the .toml out · 15 Move this step up — step 0 IN … 30 Apply IN · 31 Close IN · 32 Cutscene step type IN · 33 Cutscene step dialogue IN · 34 QPlainTextEdit[unnamed] IN · 35 actor'.
findings.user_path: Keyboard only: focus the scene rail, then press Tab repeatedly to reach a step's Edit button and the editor
findings.fix: After set_rows/set_inset, chain setTabOrder: scene bar → row tools → editor (fields, then Apply/Close) → stage. Give the preview box Qt.NoFocus.

findings.title: Undo/Redo of a scene add, duplicate or delete selects a different scene than the one it restored
findings.statement: History restores the whole buffer. Because the member name is unchanged, show_field only clamps the existing _scene index. After 'undo delete scene #1' the rail shows #0, not the restored #1. Redo of a duplicate leaves the original selected, not the copy. Redo of 'add scene' shows #2, not the re-added #3. The user has to go looking for what the history step just changed.
findings.evidence: Probe probes/x-cutscene-place/p1_scene_undo.py (real buttons + win._undo/_redo): 'del scene1 → doc._scene=0', 'undo del scenes=3 doc._scene=0 title='scene #0''; 'dup scene1 → scene #2', 'redo dup scenes=3 doc._scene=1'; 'add scene → #3', 'redo add scenes=4 doc._scene=2'. Ladder, stage and stack were otherwise consistent, with raw still pointing at the shell buffer.
findings.user_path: Cutscene tab → select scene #1 → − Scene → Ctrl+Z (or ⧉ Scene → Ctrl+Z → Ctrl+Shift+Z)
findings.fix: Have the history record carry the scene index the op touched (the cutscene_tab focus key could hold 'cutscene_tab:<k>'), and have _goto_focus pass it so the doc selects that scene.

findings.title: No keyboard path to place content or draw a region on the Place tab
findings.statement: The backdrop canvas takes Tab focus, but its keyPressEvent handles only Esc (abandon a quad being drawn) and Ctrl+0/Ctrl+1. No key moves a placement point, drops an NPC, prop, spawn or arrival, or adds a region corner, and the region menu (retarget, rotate, message, delete) opens only on right-click over a quad. Every placing action of the tab needs a mouse. The Editor forms are the only keyboard route, and the tab does not point to them.
findings.evidence: Probe probes/x-cutscene-place/p10_place_kb.py walks the focus chain on a loaded novel field: 'Load the room → Place tool → Regions tool → NPC → Prop → Spawn → Arrival → BackdropCanvas[Field backdrop] → (leaves the tab)'. Reading backdrop.py keyPressEvent (1087-1104) confirms that only Esc and Ctrl+0/1 are handled.
findings.user_path: Keyboard only: Place tab → Load the room → Tab to the canvas → try to place an NPC or draw a gateway
findings.fix: Add a keyboard cursor on the canvas (arrows move a crosshair over the floor, Enter places or adds a corner), and the context-menu key (Shift+F10) to open the region menu on the selected quad. At minimum, make the status line name the Editor form as the keyboard route.

findings.title: A 16-bit PNG opens and builds as a solid white rectangle, with no warning
findings.statement: load_image and build_image_field both call Image.open(path).convert('RGB'). Pillow converts a 16-bit greyscale PNG (mode I;16, which GIMP, Photoshop and RAW converters export) by clamping each 0-65535 sample to 255. Any normal photo therefore becomes pure white, both on the Trace canvas and in the shipped art/base.png. The user traces on a blank frame, and Generate ships a white background with exit 0.
findings.evidence: Script: probes/x-trace-e2e/p4_odd_keyboard.py (output in p4.out). A gradient 16-bit PNG whose 8-bit-equivalent mean is 94.9 gives: 'tab/build ingest convert(RGB) mean [255.0, 255.0, 255.0]', 'tab canvas pixels across the 16-bit gradient [255, 255, 255, 255]', 'CLI on 16-bit exit 0 base mean [255.0, 255.0, 255.0]'. Other odd inputs (paletted, JPEG, CMYK JPEG, 8-bit grey, RGBA, 64x64, 4000x1000, 1080x2400, 6000x4000) all ingest correctly (p1.out, p7).
findings.user_path: Export the room painting from an editor at 16 bits per channel and open it in Trace.
findings.fix: Add one shared ingest helper used by both the tab and the build: for I;16 or I modes, scale with point(lambda v: v / 257) (or numpy >> 8) before convert('RGB'). Also flatten RGBA over a known colour instead of letting it go black.

findings.title: Hand-authored and Place-tab doors and zones are invisible on the Trace canvas, so traced doors can be drawn over them with no overlap warning
findings.statement: load_project absorbs only the generator's own traced_ rows into the session, and the canvas is fed only from the session (_region_shim). A door0 or zone0 drawn in the Place tab, or written by hand, is therefore not drawn on the Trace canvas at all, not even as inert context. placedoc.region_rows' overlap law, which this tab already runs, cannot judge a new traced door against it. The author draws doors blind to the doors the project already has, the same gap P8 names for donor doors on forks, here on the Trace lane.
findings.evidence: Script: probes/x-trace-e2e/p5_shell_crosstab.py (output in p5.out), whole shell. Trace generates HALL, Place loads it, drops an NPC and draws door0, then Save All gives 'after Save All: gateways [door0]'. Back on Trace: '3. Trace regions on canvas 0 session regions 0'. Place itself shows it: '4. Place markers 2 regions 1'.
findings.user_path: Trace -> Generate -> Place: draw a door -> Save -> back to Trace -> Regions tool: the existing door is not shown.
findings.fix: Feed the file-side gateway and event rows to the canvas as locked, inert context rows. They are already invertible through the same camera (load_project does it for traced rows). Include them in the shim the overlap law judges, and keep them out of the argv.

findings.title: Every Trace Regenerate moves a Place-tab spawn back to the floor centroid; the only notice is one Output line
findings.statement: The Place tab offers Spawn on a traced project and writes [player] spawn. The regenerate merge treats spawn as generator-owned, so the next Trace Regenerate silently resets it to the vertex average. The merge names it as 'retook player.spawn' in the console, but the Trace tab's status line and the Problems verdict say nothing. The user's deliberate spawn placement is lost on any later floor tweak. Arrivals, NPCs, props and Place doors survive (verified), so spawn is the odd one out.
findings.evidence: Script: probes/x-trace-e2e/p3_reopen_crosstab.py, section B (output in p3.out). placedoc.set_spawn(data, 10, -1100) is saved, then a Trace vertex nudge and Regenerate give: 'B survived: ... spawn [-5, -833] arrival [{entrance: 1, pos: [20, -1000]}]'. The only trace is the console line 'retook (generator-owned, the session wins): player.spawn'. The Trace status reads 'Generating REOPEN -> ... ...'.
findings.user_path: Trace -> Generate -> Place: Spawn tool, click a spot -> Save -> Trace: nudge a vertex -> Regenerate.
findings.fix: Keep a file-side spawn that still lies on the new walkmesh, and retake it only when it falls off. Or at least surface 'retaken' and 'removed' in the Trace status and Problems verdict after the job.

findings.title: Trace status line stays on 'Generating X -> ... ...' forever after the job ends, success or failure
findings.statement: on_generate sets the status to 'Generating <name> -> <out> ...'. _after_generate never refreshes it: it returns early on failure and on every Regenerate, and only hands off after a clean first Generate. So the tab's own status line keeps claiming a build is in progress after an exit 0, an exit 1, or a Stop, until the next gesture. On a failed job it also hides the gesture count and the not-stamped warning.
findings.evidence: Script: p6_shell_cp1252.py (output in p6.out). After the job had exited 1: 'trace status: Generating HALL -> ...p6\hall-field ...'. Same in p3 section B after an exit-0 Regenerate: 'B trace status: ...room-field ...'.
findings.user_path: Click Generate or Regenerate, wait for the Output panel to finish, and look at the Trace tab's status line.
findings.fix: In _after_generate, always _refresh() with the verdict ('HALL regenerated' / 'Generate failed -- see Output'), then do the first-run hand-off.

findings.title: Trace authoring has no keyboard path: floor vertices, cut-out contacts and regions are mouse-only
findings.statement: The canvas takes focus (StrongFocus, in the Tab chain), but its keyPressEvent handles only Esc (cancel a pending quad) and Ctrl+0 / Ctrl+1. There is no keyboard way to add, select, nudge or delete a vertex, mark a contact, draw or reshape a region, or open the vertex or region menu. Delete, Backspace, arrows, Return and Space on the focused canvas do nothing, and Ctrl+Z on the bare tab does nothing (T26 covers Ctrl+Z inside the shell). Everything around the canvas (Open, pitch, Undo, Clear, Name, id, Generate) is reachable, so the whole core task is the one part a keyboard user cannot do.
findings.evidence: Script: probes/x-trace-e2e/p4_odd_keyboard.py (output in p4.out). 'focus chain: [Open an image..., Camera pitch, Floor tool, Undo, Clear, BackdropCanvas: Field backdrop, Field name, Field id, Generate field project...]'; 'canvas keys changed the floor? False'; 'Ctrl+Z on the canvas (no shell) changed the floor? False'.
findings.user_path: Tab into the canvas after opening a photo and try to trace or fix a vertex without the mouse.
findings.fix: Add a keyboard cursor: arrows move a crosshair, Enter adds a vertex or corner, Tab/Shift+Tab select vertices, arrows nudge the selected one (one history step per key release), Delete removes it, and the Menu key opens the region or vertex menu at the selection. The canvas already has the canvas-px seams (_commit_floor, _drag_canvas).

findings.title: The first-Generate hand-off test does not cover a real retry after a failure
findings.statement: test_first_generate_hands_the_project_to_the_shell_once calls kw['on_finished'](1) and then kw['on_finished'](0) on the SAME launch's callback. A real user retries with a second on_generate, which captures first=False because _project was set when the first job started. The test therefore passes while the retry path never opens the project (see T8).
findings.evidence: /v-trace-tab/p_doc.py: a failed first launch, then a second on_generate, then on_finished(0) with the toml present gives opened == [].
findings.fix: Replace the double callback with: on_generate > on_finished(1) > on_generate > on_finished(0) > assert opened == [toml]. This fails today, which pins the T8 fix.

findings.title: A stale async load's failure lands on the next field and re-enables Load mid-flight
findings.statement: _gen is bumped in show_none/show_field but never read, and the loader signals carry no key or generation. _on_load_failed unconditionally sets _loading=None, re-enables load_btn and writes 'Could not load the room: <msg>'. _on_loaded clears _loading and re-enables Load before its stale check. If field A's load fails after the user has switched to B and started B's load, B's status shows A's error, and Load is enabled while B is still in flight, so a second click starts a duplicate worker. A success from A is correctly cached and not applied. show_none also does not reset _loading.
findings.evidence: Code read at lines 398, 515, 562 and 600-611. I re-ran place-code/p4_widget.py part (b): 'member B status: Could not load the room: RuntimeError: A blew up | load_btn enabled while B in flight: True _loading None', after which B's own load applied normally.
findings.user_path: Load on a slow/failing room -> switch to another member -> Load -> the first load fails.
findings.fix: Emit the request key with loaded/failed (or carry it in the bundle and in a failed tuple). In both handlers, touch _loading/load_btn/status only when key == self._loading; otherwise just cache (on success) or ignore (on failure).

findings.title: The stacked-floor chooser implies a floor choice the doc cannot record
findings.statement: On a stacked walkmesh pixel, _choose_hit offers 'floor N · height … (visible/behind)', and the status echoes '· floor N'. _apply_hit writes only pos [x, z] (the schema has no floor/height key). The re-fed marker resolves its height with floor_y_at(..., eye), which picks the candidate nearest the camera. So after choosing the behind/upper floor, the marker is drawn on the other floor, at a different pixel from the click. What the menu did choose is a different plan (x,z), where the ray hits that floor, so the choice is not meaningless, but the label promises a floor binding that is not stored. A click exactly on a shared triangle edge lists the same floor twice. Which floor the engine actually seats the actor on cannot be settled offline.
findings.evidence: I re-ran place-code/p5_state.py part 1: stacked rows [(0,0,[0,721]), (1,-300,[0,1500]), (1,-300,[0,1500])] (duplicate floor-1 row). After picking floor 1 the status reads '... at (0, 1500) · floor 1', but 'marker y: [0.0] (chosen floor y was -300.0)'. I read imagefield.floor_y_at (eye-nearest candidate) and confirmed that build has no NPC floor key.
findings.user_path: A bridge/balcony field -> Place -> click where two floors overlap -> choose the 'behind' entry.
findings.fix: De-duplicate hits per floor. Reword the menu to say it picks the plan point where the ray meets that floor, and that height is resolved by the engine, or warn when the chosen (x,z) lies over more than one floor. Recording a floor would need a schema key and a build change (L).

findings.title: Verbatim forks: the donor's own tread regions are invisible to Place's overlap judge
findings.statement: region_rows (and build.region_overlap_pairs behind it) judge only the [[gateway]]/[[event]] rows in field.toml. On a VERBATIM fork the donor's real exits live only in the whole .eb, and _inject_verbatim_gateways adds the kit's new gateways below the party band, so a door drawn over a real exit gets no 'overlaps' warning on the canvas (nor from the lint, which uses the same judge). The claim overreaches for native, editable and BG-borrow forks: the importer (extract.py:622-650) writes the donor's scanned exits into field.toml as [[gateway]] rows, so those forks DO show and judge them. The gap is verbatim-only. It is a kit-wide judge limitation, not something only Place gets wrong.
findings.evidence: Read placedoc.region_rows:162-215, build.region_overlap_pairs:3944 (it reads only the raw dict), build._inject_verbatim_gateways:7065. extract.py:622-650 emits [[gateway]] blocks for non-verbatim imports. eb/pressclosure.analyze_regions:834 and guest_traversal.tread_regions:1241 exist as decoders.
findings.user_path: Open a verbatim fork, Place > Load the room > Regions, draw a gateway over the donor's real door: no overlap warning.
findings.fix: Decode the donor .eb's tread regions once per load (analyze_regions over cache_field's .eb). Feed them to the canvas as greyed, read-only rows and to the overlap judge as extra boxes. Put that in the shared judge so the lint benefits too. Verbatim-only.

findings.title: Place writes .place_backdrop.png into the user's project folder (one file for all cameras)
findings.statement: _project_backdrop saves its composite to <project dir>/.place_backdrop.png from the worker thread on every project-surface load. That puts a generated artifact into the author's source tree (it gets committed, zipped and packed with the folder). It is a dotfile, so Explorer hides it by default, and the only ignore rule is in one study folder. The real-donor lane writes to provision.cache_dir()/place/real_<id>_cam<ci>.png. Every camera shares the same filename, so concurrent or successive loads overwrite each other. It is harmless to the build, hence minor.
findings.evidence: My probe v-place-bugs/p3_backdrop.py lists the project dir after one call: ['.place_backdrop.png', 'R.field.toml', ...]. Code read at lines 340-342 versus build_surface line 365.
findings.user_path: Open any novel/traced/editable field -> Place -> Load the room -> look in the project folder.
findings.fix: Write to provision.cache_dir()/'place'/f'project_{sha1(path)[:12]}_cam{ci}.png' (pass the camera index into _project_backdrop), mirroring build_surface.

findings.title: Set message accepts an empty string: the event passes validation but has no action
findings.statement: The event quad's Set message dialog (_ask_message) returns '' when the author clears the box, and set_event_message writes message=''. build.validate's 'needs at least one action' check tests only that the key is present (build.py:1560), and _event_shows_text('') is False, so the zone builds clean and does nothing in-game. region_rows warns only for the literal '...' placeholder, so no warning shows on the canvas either.
findings.evidence: My probe v-place-bugs/p_misc.py: after set_event_message(d,0,''), 'empty msg warn: None | shows text: False'. I read build.py 1555-1564 and 6376-6380.
findings.user_path: Regions -> right-click an event quad -> Set message -> clear the text -> OK.
findings.fix: Treat an empty or whitespace result in _on_region_reword as cancel (or re-prompt). Better, also make build.validate count a message only when it is non-blank, which covers the Editor form path too, and have region_rows warn on a blank message.

findings.title: Gateway target entry has no registration/band check, and retargeting a worldmap door converts it to an int
findings.statement: The 'to field' spin box (0..32767) and the Set gateway target dialog (1..32767) accept any id, and region_rows warns only for to<=0. An id in the reserved 9000-9012 world-location hole, or one that is neither a stock field nor a field registered anywhere, builds cleanly and black-screens in-game. The claim is overstated where it says 3101-3999 and 9900-29999 'cannot load': those ids are reachable when a field is registered there (fldMapNo is Int16), so the real defect is the missing check that the target exists, not a band rule. The right-click menu also offers Set gateway target on a to="worldmap" door. The dialog starts at 1 and cannot express 'worldmap', and accepting it silently turns the door into a field warp.
findings.evidence: My probe v-place-bugs/p_misc.py: to 9005 / 3500 / 20000 all warn: None (only 0 warns); a worldmap row shows no warning, the dialog's initial value would be 1, and set_gateway_target(…,100) yields to=100. I read build.py 1490-1500: validate also checks only for <=0.
findings.user_path: Regions -> draw a gateway with a typo id, or right-click a worldmap door -> Set gateway target.
findings.fix: Warn in region_rows for 9000-9012 and for an id that is neither in reference/field-manifest.tsv nor a field of the open project or a live registration. Hide or refuse Set gateway target on a worldmap door, or offer a 'worldmap' choice.

findings.title: place_prop mints duplicate names after a delete (prop{len(lst)})
findings.statement: place_prop names a new prop f'prop{len(lst)}' instead of using _fresh_name, as gateways and events do (NPCs use fresh_npc_name). After any prop is removed, the next drop reuses a live name: placing two props, deleting prop0 and placing again gives ['prop1', 'prop1']. The tree shows two identical rows, the status 'place prop' cannot say which one, and build's duplicate-name lint does not cover props.
findings.evidence: My probe v-place-bugs/p_misc.py prints props: ['prop1', 'prop1']. place-code/p2_ops.py and place-ux-look/probe1.py reproduce the same result.
findings.user_path: Place two props -> delete prop0 in the Editor -> place another prop.
findings.fix: nm = _fresh_name('prop', lst) and return f'place prop {nm}'. Optionally add 'prop' to the build's duplicate-name lint loop.

findings.title: The loading status prints the raw source tuple, and the copy still assumes a donor
findings.statement: Since the bundle key became (source_tuple, cam), on_load formats key[0] as if it were a donor int. The status reads "Loading field #('real', 351) (camera 0) — extracting + compositing…", or on a novel field a Python tuple with a doubled-backslash Windows path. This is the only feedback during a load that can take seconds. The idle hints (lines 529, 885-889: 'Open a field (a fork of a real room)…', "the donor's art, camera, and walkmesh") and the Load button tooltip ('Extract the donor's camera…') still describe the pre-Rung-7d donor-only lane.
findings.evidence: I re-ran place-ux-look/probe1.py: '1. status while loading: "Loading field #(\'real\', 351) (camera 0)…"' and '1b. … #(\'project\', \'C:\\\\Users…demo.field.toml\') …'. The lines are visible in the code read.
findings.user_path: Open any field -> Place -> Load the room.
findings.fix: Format from the source kind: real -> f'Loading donor field #{ref}…', project -> f'Loading {Path(ref).name}…', with the camera appended only when n_cams > 1. Reword the idle hints and the tooltip to cover both lanes.

findings.title: The verbatim-fork tooltip sticks on Spawn/Arrival for every later field
findings.statement: _sync_modes sets the 'a verbatim fork runs the donor's own entry sequence — spawn/arrival rows are ignored on it' tooltip on the Spawn and Arrival radios only in its verbatim branch and never clears it. After any verbatim fork has been shown, those radios are re-enabled on later non-verbatim fields, but their tooltip still says the clicks will be ignored, so an enabled control claims it is dead.
findings.evidence: I re-ran place-code/p5_state.py part 3 and place-ux-look/probe1.py 3a/3b: 'non-verbatim spawn enabled: True tooltip: a verbatim fork runs the donor's own entry sequence — spawn/'. Code read at lines 794-814.
findings.user_path: Open a verbatim fork in Place -> open an ordinary/novel field -> hover Spawn.
findings.fix: At the top of _sync_modes, set both radios' tooltips to a neutral description (or ''), and override them only in the verbatim branch.

findings.title: The canvas hint pill is static ('click the floor' in every mode) and sits over the art's bottom-right, covering handles and labels
findings.statement: The pill text is set once in the constructor and never changes (no setText anywhere). Trace Regions, Trace Cut-outs, Place Regions and Place's refused and bare states all read 'Ctrl+scroll zooms · Ctrl+0 fits · click the floor', even when the gesture is four corner clicks or the object's base, or there is nothing to click. Right-click/Esc as cancel gestures appear only in Place's status line. The pill is pinned to the viewport's bottom-right over the art, which is where the near floor edge, doors and contacts live. In the snaps it covers zone0's corner 3 in trace-regions, and at 150% it covers the fg0 contact diamond and its 'fg0 · z 1073' label. It is mouse-transparent, so a press goes through to a handle the user cannot see. The status lines do carry mode-correct guidance, which limits the harm.
findings.evidence: Code read: one QLabel construction at line 116, with no later setText on _hint. Viewed review-ctp/mist-100/trace-regions-canvas_mist_100.png (pill over zone0's corner 3 and spill) and mist-150/trace-contacts_mist_150.png (pill over the fg0 diamond and label). The 4.41:1 contrast number was not re-measured.
findings.user_path: Trace or Place: switch to Regions. The pill still says 'click the floor' and hides the bottom-right of the art.
findings.fix: Add set_hint(text) and set a per-mode string from each set_*_mode (regions: 'click 4 corners · Esc/right-click cancels · drag a quad to move'; contact: 'click the object's base'). Hide the pill when there is no camera, and fade it after the first gesture or reserve its band in _fit.

findings.title: Place's refused state looks live: disabled radios keep full-contrast labels over an empty frame
findings.statement: On a protected field (a bundled example or an installed copy), _sync_modes disables both tools, every radio and the spinners. Only 'Load the room' visibly recedes. The NPC/Prop/Spawn/Arrival radio labels render in full $text, exactly like enabled ones; only their indicator rings mute. The checked 'Place' segment keeps its raised pill, and the 'Regions' segment is muted, which is the same colour an enabled unchecked segment has. Under them sits a large empty frame with the 'click the floor' pill. The one signal is the warn line at the bottom.
findings.evidence: Pixel sampling of mist-100/place-refused_mist_100.png at 3840 px: the brightest pixel in the NPC and Spawn label boxes is (233,230,220) = $text, while the disabled Load button's text is (159,173,196) = $muted. style.py has QRadioButton::indicator:disabled rules (380-386) but no QRadioButton:disabled text colour. The #railSeg rule (822) has no :disabled rule.
findings.user_path: Open a bundled example (e.g. examples/vivi-hut) and go to Author > Place.
findings.fix: Add 'QCheckBox:disabled, QRadioButton:disabled { color: $muted; }' and a #railSeg:disabled rule (see T28). When _blocked is set, show a centred empty-state message in the canvas, with a 'Save a copy…' action if one exists.

findings.title: BackdropCanvas labels and corner indices overprint into an unreadable cluster (no de-collision)
findings.statement: Each region gets a centroid label at a fixed (6,-16) screen offset, and in region mode four corner squares with index labels. Markers add labels at (7,-15). Nothing de-collides them, unlike StageCanvas._decollide_labels in behaviordoc. When zones sit near the back of a room they compress to a few pixels and the text overprints: in the light regions snap, 'door0 → 4005' is split by a corner handle, 'zone0' and 'zone1' read 'one0' and 'one1' under handles and warn glyphs, and '2door1 → 4005' merges an index into the label. The fixture worsens the crowding, because its camera puts every zone in the back sliver of the art (see P28). But the mechanism is real: any far-back or adjacent zones produce it.
findings.evidence: Read light-100/place-regions-canvas_light_100.png: the cluster around (780-1420, 290-490) shows '2door1 → 4005', 'one0', 'one1', and 'door0' cut by handle 1. Code: backdrop.py:642-656, 681-684, 709-712, with no collision pass anywhere in BackdropCanvas.
findings.user_path: Place or Trace > Regions: draw two or three zones near the far wall.
findings.fix: Show corner indices only for the hovered or last-touched quad (the walk-out chevron already shows order). Give labels the plate from P20. Add a cheap greedy pass after _rebuild/_fit/zoom that nudges or hides a label whose rect intersects an earlier one, keeping the full text in the tooltip.

findings.title: Place's empty-state, Load tooltip and pre-load prompt still describe a donor-only, fork-only tab
findings.statement: Since Rung 7d, Place accepts novel, composed, traced and `ff9mapkit new` fields (build_surface_from_project). Its text still says otherwise. The no-field note (show_none:529 and _refresh:885) reads 'Open a field (a fork of a real room) and come back — or fork one on the Import tab'. The Load tooltip (418) reads 'Extract the donor's camera + walkmesh and composite its background'. The pre-load prompt (888) reads 'the donor's art, camera, and walkmesh arrive together'. A from-scratch author is told to go and fork something. The refusal comes from editor.model.protected_reason:163 ('-- edit a copy, or scaffold one with `ff9mapkit new`'): it mixes an ASCII '--' with the em dash Place prefixes, and it names a CLI command, not File > New Field.
findings.evidence: Read placedoc.py:418, 529, 885-889 and editor/model.py:163. The mist-100/place-refused snap's warn line reads 'Placement is off here — that is a bundled example -- edit a copy, or scaffold one with `ff9mapkit new`.'
findings.user_path: Open Place with no field, or with a File > New Field project before loading.
findings.fix: Reword the empty state to name every lane. Make the Load tooltip and prompt branch on self._source[0] ('real' says 'donor #N's art', 'project' says 'this field's own art'). Change the refusal wording in Place only (prefix your own GUI phrasing, e.g. 'use File ▸ New Field or save a copy'), or add a GUI variant. protected_reason is also spent by the editor and CLI, so do not reword it at the source.

findings.title: Place mode radios have no tooltips; Spawn vs Arrival vs entrance and the minted defaults are never explained
findings.statement: The NPC/Prop/Spawn/Arrival radios get a tooltip only in the verbatim-refusal branch of _sync_modes, and that tooltip is never cleared when a non-verbatim field is fed afterwards. On a normal field, nothing explains that Spawn is the default entry point while Arrival is a per-door landing keyed by the source gateway's entrance number. Nothing says each NPC is minted as a dialogue-less Vivi named npcN (place_npc:67), or that each prop is a 'barrel' (55, 74). The post-drop note ('place NPC npc0 at (x, z) · floor 0') does not say where to give it a model or words.
findings.evidence: placedoc.py:444-451 (no setToolTip on the radios), 805-810 (the only tooltip, set on the verbatim path and never reset), 55/67/74 (defaults), 856-858 (the note).
findings.user_path: Place tab on any field: hover the mode radios, place an NPC.
findings.fix: Set a one-line tooltip per radio at construction. Restore it when the field is not verbatim; today the verbatim text sticks after switching fields. Append '— give it a model/words in Editor ▸ NPCs' to the NPC and prop drop note.

findings.title: Regions: the first corner of a new zone cannot be placed inside an existing zone; the click is silently swallowed
findings.statement: With no pending corners, a left press over any regionquad or regionedge item starts a whole-quad drag. A release within slop ends it unchanged (just a rebuild) and never reaches the corner-append path. No corner is added, no click_refused is emitted and no status text appears. Starting an event zone whose first corner lies inside a larger gateway or event zone is therefore impossible until the user discovers that the first corner must be outside every quad; later corners work anywhere. No test or study doc records this as intended.
findings.evidence: probe2.py section D rerun: 'pending corners after a click inside region 0: 0 drawn 0 changed 0 refused []'. grep of the backdrop, tracedoc and placedoc tests finds nothing pinning the behaviour.
findings.user_path: Trace or Place > Regions with one zone drawn: click inside it to start a second zone. Nothing happens.
findings.fix: Treat an rquad drag released within _CLICK_SLOP_PX (unchanged quad) as a corner click, falling through to the append path. Only regionpt handles keep absolute priority.

findings.title: The Place tab has no user documentation beyond one sentence
findings.statement: The only user-facing mention of the Place tab in ff9mapkit/docs or docsite is one paragraph in S3 Gateways: the tab's Regions tool is 'the visual route (no separate tutorial yet...)'. docsite/pages/what-can-i-do.md has no Place entry. Load the room, the verbatim spawn/arrival refusal, the stacked-floor menu, the walk-out edge (corners 0→1), the right-click rotate/retarget/reword/delete, Esc to cancel, the overlap and dead-zone warnings, and Undo are recorded only in studies/click-authoring/PLAN.md, which is not user documentation.
findings.evidence: Case-insensitive grep over ff9mapkit/docs, docsite and ff9mapkit/README.md for 'Place tab|Load the room|Regions tool' returned only s3-gateways.md:69-71.
findings.user_path: A user looking for how to use Author > Place.
findings.fix: Add a short 'Place content on the art' tutorial page: Load, the four modes, Regions gestures, refusals and warnings. Link it from what-can-i-do.md and from the S3 note.

findings.title: A drawn gateway with no target, or a drawn event, could prompt immediately via the existing dialog seams
findings.statement: _on_region_drawn writes a gateway with to=0 when the 'to field' spinner shows its '?' special value, and writes every event with message '...'. Both are then flagged on the canvas (Field(0) black screen / literal '...' popup), and the fix takes a right-click > Set gateway target / Set message. This is the DEFAULT-VALUE LAW's 'loudly invalid' option working as designed, so it is not a bug. But the instance dialogs _ask_field_id and _ask_message already exist behind test seams. Calling them right after the draw, only when to == 0 or for an event, with cancel keeping today's placeholder, removes a two-step repair from the most common Regions flow. Trace already captures the event text up front (ev_msg box), so prompting is consistent with the sibling tab.
findings.evidence: placedoc.py:701-714 (to=0 only appends a hint to the note), 736-792 (dialog seams), 199-205 (the warnings). tracedoc.py:177 captures the message before the draw.
findings.user_path: Place > Regions: draw a gateway without first setting 'to field'.
findings.fix: In _on_region_drawn: if gateway and to == 0, call _ask_field_id(0) and, if accepted, set_gateway_target in the SAME undo step (one on_edit). For an event, call _ask_message(''). Cancel keeps the current behaviour.

findings.title: A camera pick carried over by member name makes Load never apply (stuck on 'Loading…')
findings.statement: _cam_pick is keyed by member name only and is never cleared, not even in show_none. If a previous field with the same name had camera 1 picked and the newly fed field has fewer cameras, on_load requests (source, 1). The builder clamps to camera 0 and returns cam_index 0. _on_loaded caches the result under (source, 0), sees 0 != _cam_index() (1), treats it as 'user moved on', and drops it without refreshing the status. Every further Load misses the cache under (source, 1), rebuilds, and drops again. The room never appears, the status stays on 'Loading … (camera 1)', and the camera combo stays hidden (it is synced only in _apply_bundle and hidden for one camera), so nothing in the UI recovers short of a restart. Reaching it needs a same-named member across projects (as in P5) after a multi-camera pick, so it is an edge case, but a dead end when hit.
findings.evidence: My probe v-place-bugs/p29_cam.py (PlaceDoc with build_surface_from_project patched to clamp like the real one): project 1 room A with 2 cams, pick camera 1 -> applied. Project 2 room A with 1 cam -> 'Load #1: applied=False bundles cams=[0] status="Loading field #(…) (camera 1" cam_box visible=False', and the same for Load #2.
findings.user_path: Open a multi-camera room 'A', pick camera 1 in Place -> open another project whose room 'A' has one camera -> Place -> Load.
findings.fix: Key _cam_pick on the source (or the path), and clear it in show_none. In on_load or _on_loaded, clamp the pick to the bundle's n_cams and store the clamped index back (or compare against min(pick, n_cams-1)), so a clamped result is applied.

findings.title: The Inspector's Contents rollup goes stale after a Place drop while the tree count updates
findings.statement: _on_place_edit refreshes the member's tree object rows (so 'Props (1)' appears) but never re-runs the Inspector. Place, unlike Cutscene/Behavior, keeps the ordinary field card in the right column, so after a drop the tree and the Inspector on the same screen disagree: the tree says Props (1) while CONTENTS still reads '1 NPC'. _rollup (shell.py:8626) does count props, so a re-render would fix it. The card corrects itself on the next tree selection.
findings.evidence: I viewed tools/scroll_out/gui_snaps/review-ctp/mist-100/place-fork_mist_100.png. The tree shows 'NPCs (1)' and 'Props (1)', the status line says 'place prop at (300, 1700) · floor 0', and the Inspector CONTENTS shows only '1 NPC'. That state was produced by gui_snap.snap_place driving the real _apply_hit -> on_edit -> _on_place_edit path (gui_snap.py:1921-1923), so it is a real user path. grep confirms _rollup iterates over 'prop'.
findings.user_path: Place tab -> Load -> place a prop -> look at the Inspector column.
findings.fix: At the end of _on_place_edit, re-render the Inspector for the current tree item (the existing _inspect/select path with tree signals blocked). The same applies to the Cutscene/Behavior edit hooks if they ever show the field card.

findings.title: Player spawn is the vertex mean: off the floor for strongly concave traces
findings.statement: The generated [player].spawn is the arithmetic mean of the un-projected floor vertices. For a strongly concave trace (an L, or a U around a counter) that point lies outside both the traced polygon and the outset walkmesh. Image-field generation and the Trace tab give no warning, and the tab never draws the spawn. The claim's 'no warning' is overstated, though. build._validate_content_placement (build.py:4996-5000) warns 'player spawn ... is off the walkmesh -- you'll start off the floor' at Build/Deploy. The author is told, just late and away from the Trace canvas. Most photo floors are convex trapezoids, so this needs a deliberately concave trace.
findings.evidence: Re-ran probe_spawn.py: 'L (canvas) spawn (-225, -850) inside traced floor: False inside walkmesh: False'; 'U (canvas) spawn (-10, -539) ... False'. Read build.py:4931-5004: an off-mesh spawn produces a build warning. Could not run a full build here (no templates in this fresh worktree).
findings.user_path: Trace an L-shaped floor, Generate, Deploy. The build warns that the spawn is off the walkmesh; Warp puts the player off the floor.
findings.fix: Choose an interior spawn: the centroid of the largest triangle from triangulate(), or an area-weighted centroid checked with point-in-polygon, falling back to a triangle centroid. Optionally draw a spawn marker on the Trace canvas. The suggested fix is sound.

findings.title: outset_polygon: no miter limit; narrow notches fold into overlapping triangles
findings.statement: The geometry is as reported. The miter offset has no limit: a 5-degree corner moves 1100 world units. A concave notch narrower than 2x48u inverts after the outset (the walls cross), and triangulate then emits overlapping triangles whose summed area exceeds the polygon area. Nothing detects this before walkmesh.obj is written, and the build's _validate_walkmesh_geometry flags only zero-area triangles. The reach is narrower than the claim implies. At the default camera, 96u is about 16 canvas px at mid-depth, not 'a few px', so it takes a deliberate slit-like notch or a very sharp spike. A consecutive duplicate vertex cannot come from canvas clicks; it can arrive only through the CLI --floor or the load_project inversion. Collinear runs end up as zero-area triangles, which the build already warns about.
findings.evidence: Re-ran probe_geom.py and probe_tri.py: '5 deg ... (2000, 0) -> (3099, -48) moved 1100'; 60u notch outset '(1482, 2048), (1482, 348), (1518, 348), (1518, 2048)' (crossed); 'Uout ... tri sum 6625872 poly 6550416' (overlap). Duplicate vertex: outset leaves (1000,0) unshifted. Read build.py:5064-5083: only degenerate (zero-area) triangles are warned.
findings.user_path: Trace a floor with a very thin inward notch (around a pillar base), or a very acute far tip, then Generate. The walkmesh has overlapping triangles or a long spike.
findings.fix: Drop consecutive duplicate and near-collinear vertices first. Bevel any miter longer than about 2d. After the outset, check that the polygon is simple and that the triangle-area sum equals the polygon area, and raise ImageFieldError naming the vertex if not. The suggested fix is sound.

findings.title: Self-intersecting floor trace is accepted and triangulated over its hull
findings.statement: Neither the Trace canvas (backdrop.py:1203-1206 appends every click), the TraceDoc ready gate (good>=3, bad==0) nor build_image_field checks that the floor polygon is simple. For a crossed outline (bowtie) the signed area is about 0, so _as_ccw does not re-wind it, and the ear-clipper and fan fallback emit triangles covering the whole square. The walkmesh then includes floor the author never traced. The outline is drawn on the canvas, so a crossed trace is visible to the author before Generate; the realistic route is a vertex drag across an edge during refinement. The collinear 3-click case produces a zero-area triangle, which build._validate_walkmesh_geometry already warns about at build time.
findings.evidence: probe_geom.py: bowtie 'signed area 0.0 faces [(3, 0, 1), (1, 2, 3)] tri area sum 1000000.0' against 500000 drawn. probe_build.py: 'bowtie floor builds silently? built: 4 verts 2 faces (no refusal)'. build.py:5078 warns on degenerate triangles only.
findings.user_path: Trace 4 floor points in a crossing order, or drag a vertex across the opposite edge, then Generate.
findings.fix: Add an O(n^2) segment-crossing check plus a non-zero-area check in build_image_field (ImageFieldError), and mirror it in TraceDoc._refresh as a Generate gate that highlights the crossing edge. This can share the simplicity check with T4.

findings.title: A region pushed above the horizon by a pitch change disappears from the canvas, but the tooltip says to right-click it
findings.statement: _region_shim leaves out any region with a corner above the current horizon, and _refresh_regions feeds only the shim rows to the canvas. A gateway or event quad drawn high on the photo at the default pitch 26 disappears from the canvas when the author lowers the pitch (for example to 10, horizon y 141.7). The region stays in the session, Generate is disabled, and the Generate tooltip tells the author to 'reshape or delete it (right-click the quad)', but there is no quad to right-click. Floor vertices in the same state stay on the canvas and are drawn red. The way out is to slide the pitch back, which brings the quad back, or to press Undo. Nothing is lost and no wrong bytes can be written, so this is friction plus a misleading tooltip, not a major bug.
findings.evidence: My own probe /v-trace-tab/p_t6.py drew a real event zone through _on_region_drawn at pitch 26 (corners at canvas y 100-140), then set the pitch to 10. Result: 'fed 0 canvas 0 gen False', with status '1 region · 1 above the horizon'. Floor vertices above the horizon remained ('2 above the horizon (red)'). The reporter's probe injects into _regions directly but gives the same result: 'pitch 12 rows fed: 0'. Setting the pitch back restores the quad.
findings.user_path: Trace tab > Regions tool > draw a door near the top of the photo > lower the Pitch slider > the quad vanishes > the Generate tooltip says to right-click it.
findings.fix: Keep above-horizon rows in the canvas feed, drawn at their stored canvas px with a 'bad' flag (red, like bad vertices) that the law judge skips, so right-click Delete still works. The cheaper option is to change the tooltip and status to 'slide the pitch back to see it, or Undo'.

findings.title: Field name is not validated: a bad name leaves a half-written project and prints a traceback
findings.statement: TraceDoc passes name_box text straight to --name, and build_image_field uses it as the filename <out>/<name>.field.toml. Its comment says 'every refusal has passed: NOW touch the disk', but the filename is never checked. walkmesh.obj and art/ are written first, then the toml write raises. On Windows, a name containing ? " : * gives OSError [Errno 22], and a name containing / gives FileNotFoundError. OSError is not in the CLI's except tuple (cli.py:3671), so the Output panel shows a raw traceback. On an in-place Regenerate this replaces walkmesh.obj and art under the old, unchanged toml. The Editor's own name spec (editor/forms.py:79) and hub._NAME_RE allow only letters, digits and underscore. Authors are not likely to type such a name, so this is minor.
findings.evidence: I re-ran trace-code/probe_build.py. Names 'A"B' and 'Q?X' raise OSError [Errno 22] and 'sub/dir' raises FileNotFoundError, each leaving ['art', 'art\\base.png', 'walkmesh.obj'] on disk. I read imagefield.py:1104-1111 (the write order) and cli.py:3671 (the except tuple).
findings.user_path: Trace tab > type a name such as 'Room?' in Name > Generate.
findings.fix: Validate the name once, with the shared ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$ rule (hub._NAME_RE), in two places: in build_image_field before any write, raising ImageFieldError, and in TraceDoc.on_generate as a status error.

findings.title: Generate sets up the project when the job starts: a failed first Generate leaves the tab armed, and the status never settles
findings.statement: on_generate sets _project, sets _stamped=True and writes the .trace.json sidecar as soon as run_job accepts the job, before the CLI has run. _after_generate returns early on failure and never refreshes the status. There are three effects. (1) After any Generate, successful or not, the Trace status line keeps saying 'Generating <name> -> <out> …' until the next gesture. (2) After a failed first Generate, the button reads 'Regenerate PICTURE — in place' for a project that does not exist, and the not-stamped warning is hidden. (3) When the author retries and it succeeds, first is False, so on_generated never fires and the project is not opened in the Editor or fed to Place (the rung-7d hand-off). The existing test (test_first_generate_hands_the_project_to_the_shell_once) misses this because it calls on_finished(1) and then on_finished(0) on the SAME launch, which is not a real retry. No data is lost and the in-place retry writes to the right folder, so the severity is minor rather than major.
findings.evidence: My probe /v-trace-tab/p_doc.py: after on_finished(2), 'btn= Regenerate PICTURE — in place stamped= True status= Generating PICTURE →'. Then a second on_generate followed by on_finished(0), with the toml present: 'opened: []', and the status still reads 'Generating…'. After a successful regenerate the status also still reads 'Generating…'.
findings.user_path: Trace tab > first Generate fails (for example a floor beyond the Int16 bound) > fix it > Generate again > the project never opens in the Editor, and the status keeps saying Generating.
findings.fix: Keep the pending {out, name, fid} in a local captured by on_finished. In _after_generate, commit _project and _stamped only when code==0, and work out 'first' from 'no successful generate yet'. Always call _refresh with a verdict: 'Generated -> <out>' or 'Generate failed — see Output'. Change the test to do a real second launch.

findings.title: Traced gateway/event zones are not Int16-checked; build fails later with struct.error
findings.statement: Floor vertices are checked against the Int16 world bound (imagefield.py:1039), but _zone_world does not check gateway or event zone corners. At the default pitch 26 the horizon is above the frame, so the canvas accepts every pixel. Any region corner in the top ~18 canvas px (of 448) un-projects to |z| > 32767. Generate writes that zone into the toml, and the failure only appears later at build, as struct.error from content/gateway.py:61's '<hh' pack, far from the cause. The reach is narrow: only a region drawn at the very top of the image (for example a far hallway door) at a shallow pitch.
findings.evidence: probe_build.py 'gateway zone near the horizon': built; zone [[-15694, 204556], ...]. My sweep at pitch 26: the first in-bound row is y=18 (z=31755); at pitch 40 every row is in bound. content/gateway.py:61 does struct.pack_into('<hh', ..., int(x), int(z)) with no range check, and grep finds no zone bound check in build.py.
findings.user_path: Trace tab at the default pitch: draw a gateway whose far corners are within ~18px of the top of the photo, then Generate (succeeds) and Deploy (struct.error).
findings.fix: In _zone_world, apply the same +-32767 bound to each corner and raise an ImageFieldError naming the zone. Mirror it in the Trace region judge so the corner is refused at click time.

findings.title: A project with a sidecar cannot be opened once its source photo is moved or deleted
findings.statement: load_project uses the folder's .trace.json whenever one exists. load_trace then calls load_image(data['image']) with the ABSOLUTE photo path recorded at Generate time, and the project's own art/base.png is never tried. If the source photo is deleted or moved, or the project is opened on another machine, the explicit Open fails with 'Could not open X.field.toml: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: <photo path>'. The message names the toml, not the missing photo, and offers no way to locate it. On the pristine auto-offer path the exception is swallowed and the path is remembered as rejected, so the open field silently never loads into Trace. The backfill path, used when no sidecar exists, would have worked from art/base.png. Deleting the sidecar is a workaround the author would not discover.
findings.evidence: I re-ran trace-code/probe_doc.py section 6 (a valid build_image_field project plus a sidecar, then the photo unlinked). Pristine auto-load gives 'image None project None rejected True'. Explicit Open gives 'Could not open MV.field.toml: [Errno 2] No such file or directory …tmp_photo.png'.
findings.user_path: Generate a traced project > delete or move the source photo (for example from Downloads) > later open the project's field.toml in Trace, or show Trace with that field open.
findings.fix: In load_trace, try the recorded path, then the photo's name beside the sidecar, then <sidecar dir>/art/base.png (art/base.png is the exact crop, so pixels map 1:1), and show a warn note when falling back. Or catch the failure in load_project and continue with the backfill branch.

findings.title: Clear acts only on the floor even when the Regions or Cut-outs tool is active; the Undo tooltip leaves out regions
findings.statement: on_clear empties only _floor, and the Clear button is enabled only while a floor exists. The button sits at the end of the tool row next to whichever tool cluster is showing. With the Regions tool active (Gateway/Event radios visible), 'Clear' is enabled whenever a floor exists, and clicking it wipes the FLOOR while every region stays. One Undo brings the floor back. There is no gesture that clears all regions or all cut-outs. The Undo tooltip says 'the last vertex or cut-out gesture', although it also undoes region gestures. The Clear tooltip ('Remove every traced vertex') is accurate, so the label in context misleads, but nothing is lost.
findings.evidence: My probe /v-trace-tab/p_doc.py with the tools set to 'regions': 'clear enabled: True label: Clear', then on_clear gives 'floor 0 regions 1'. trace-code/probe_doc.py section 2 shows that with only regions and cut-outs left, Clear is disabled. Tooltips are at tracedoc.py:186 and :190.
findings.user_path: Trace tab > Regions tool > click Clear expecting the zones to go > the floor trace disappears instead.
findings.fix: Scope Clear to the active tool, with the label following the tool ('Clear floor' / 'Clear regions' / 'Clear cut-outs'), as one undoable gesture. Change the Undo tooltip to 'the last gesture (vertex, cut-out or region)'.

findings.title: A new photo keeps the previous project's Name and Field id, so a second traced room deploys over the first
findings.statement: load_image resets the trace, project, distance and fov, but not name_box or id_box. Every new tab starts at PICTURE / 30058. If an author traces photo B after generating project A, or simply keeps the defaults for both, B is generated with A's name and id into a different folder. Nothing compares the id against previous Trace projects or the live registrations. The reporter called this an EventDB collision; the real consequence is narrower. deploy_field into the same folder at the same id reverts that slot's prior deploy, so deploying B silently replaces A in the game. A's project files stay intact and redeploying A restores it. A separate small point: widgets.BAND_HINT ('Custom band 4000–32767') does not mention the 9000-9012 reserved hole that pack.check_custom_id rejects.
findings.evidence: My probe /v-trace-tab/p_doc.py: set ROOMA/30500, then load_image(photo), and the boxes still read 'ROOMA 30500'. trace-code/probe_doc.py section 4: the second argv carries 'ROOMA', '30500' with --out …other-field. I read widgets.py:365 and pack.py:87-91.
findings.user_path: Trace tab > generate room A > Open another photo > Generate with the boxes untouched > deploy both > the first room is gone in-game.
findings.fix: In load_image for a NEW photo (not load_trace or load_project), default the name to the photo stem cleaned to [A-Za-z0-9_] and upper-cased. Suggest the next free scratch id, or at least warn in the status when the id equals the last generated project's id. Add the reserved hole to BAND_HINT.

findings.title: Canvas-frame cut-outs are misread as snips; the picker says 'full canvas'
findings.statement: The classification rule is deliberate. studies/click-authoring/PLAN.md:131-133 and :180-183 record 'a photo-aspect PNG fills the frame REGISTERED; anything else is a SNIP' and 'equal aspect = aligned, that is the whole rule'. test_workspace_tracedoc.py:214/388 pin it. So a small same-aspect crop being registered is by design: it is what the owner's rule says. The real defect is the canvas-frame case. The cut-out picker (tracedoc._ask_cutout title: 'full canvas, alpha'), the CLI --foreground help and the HTML tracer all tell the author to make a full-CANVAS PNG. The CLI build would register such a PNG 1:1, since it cover-crops each fg to the canvas. On any photo whose aspect is not 384:448, though, TraceDoc treats that 1536x1792 or 384x448 PNG as a snip and shrinks it, to 229x268 canvas px on a 4000x3000 photo.
findings.evidence: Re-ran probe_doc.py section 5: '120x160 snip on a 1200x1600 photo -> full' (matches the documented rule); '1536x1792 canvas-frame cut-out on a 4000x3000 photo -> snip preview size 229 x 268'. Read PLAN.md:130-136 and 176-183, and _ask_cutout at tracedoc.py:1126.
findings.user_path: Trace a 4:3 photo, add a cut-out made at canvas size (as the picker's 'full canvas' wording suggests), and see it shrunk to a small snip.
findings.fix: Also register a PNG whose aspect is 384:448 (the build's own frame), and reword the picker and tooltips to say 'a copy of the photo (same frame), alpha'. Keep the photo-aspect rule. Do not switch to exact-size matching, which would break the owner's documented rule.

findings.title: Renaming then Regenerating writes a second field.toml; hand content stays in the orphan
findings.statement: An in-place Regenerate takes 'out' from self._project, but takes the name from the still-editable name_box (no lock, no validator). After the Name is changed, build_image_field looks for out/<NEW>.field.toml, finds nothing to merge, and writes a fresh toml next to the old one. Both have the same field id. Every hand-authored table (NPCs, arrivals, Place doors) stays only in the old file, which the Editor and Place tab still have open. The new file is not opened (regenerates never call on_generated). No data is destroyed, but the project is split, and a deploy of the new toml ships without the hand content.
findings.evidence: probe_build.py: "kept on rename: [] ; tomls in folder: ['M.field.toml', 'RENAMED.field.toml']". Read tracedoc.py:823-836: name comes from name_box.text() while out comes from self._project; name_box is never disabled (grep on name_box).
findings.user_path: Generate a project, change the Name box, click Regenerate. The folder now holds two field.tomls.
findings.fix: Once the project is armed, either lock the Name box (with a tooltip explaining why), or on a changed name merge from the existing <old>.field.toml and rename it. Locking is the smaller, safer change.

findings.title: The auto-offer loads a broken project halfway and silently: the photo shows, no project is set up, no message
findings.statement: load_project calls load_image(base) before reading walkmesh.obj and the occluder comments. If a later step raises (walkmesh.obj missing or unreadable, or fewer than 3 'v' lines), the tab is left showing the project's art with an empty trace and the first-run teach status, and no project is set up. On the pristine auto-offer path (offer_project) the exception is swallowed and the path is remembered as rejected, so the author sees no reason. A Generate from there starts a NEW '<base>-field' project. On the explicit Open path the error is shown, but the half-loaded art stays. Broken projects like this are rare, so the severity is minor.
findings.evidence: I re-ran trace-code/probe_doc.py section 7 (a real build_image_field project with walkmesh.obj deleted, then offer_project): 'image: …noobj\\art\\base.png | project: None | status: Click the floor's outline in order…'. This is a valid user-reachable state: show the Trace tab while that field is open.
findings.user_path: Open a traced project whose walkmesh.obj is missing in the Editor > show the Trace tab > the art appears with an empty trace and no explanation.
findings.fix: Read and validate the obj ring (and the toml tables) before load_image, so every refusal comes before any state is touched, as the existing 'Honest refusals FIRST' block intends. On the auto-offer path, show the refusal as a muted status note.

findings.title: image-field CLI prints a hard-coded '--id 30058' deploy hint and does not validate --id
findings.statement: _cmd_image_field always prints 'Deploy + walk it: py tools/deploy_field.py <toml> --id 30058 (then ~ -> Warp 30058)', whatever --id was given. deploy_field's --id decides the slot, so a terminal user who copies the hint deploys into 30058, possibly another session's scratch slot on the shared install. The GUI Trace tab runs this same CLI, so when its id is not 30058 the Output panel shows this wrong line next to the GUI's correct ok_next hint. The parser (cli.py:9981) accepts any int with default 4003 and does no pack.check_custom_id, so 9000-9012, real ids and ids above 32767 pass Generate. build.py:1300-1308 catches some of these later, at build.
findings.evidence: Read cli.py:3694 (literal 30058) and cli.py:9981. probe_argv.py: '--id 9005 accepted by the parser: 9005'. The GUI path validates through pack.check_custom_id (tracedoc.py:819) and runs the same CLI, so its stdout carries the wrong hint.
findings.user_path: py -m ff9mapkit image-field photo.png --floor ... --out X --id 30777, then copy the printed deploy line. It deploys to 30058.
findings.fix: Print args.id in the hint, and call pack.check_custom_id(args.id) before building (return 2 with its message).

findings.title: EXIF orientation ignored on photo ingest; 16-bit grey PNGs go white
findings.statement: load_image, build_image_field (imagefield.py:1046), auto_floor (:622) and write_trace_html (:828) all call Image.open(...).convert('RGB') without ImageOps.exif_transpose. A portrait phone JPEG stored landscape with Orientation=6 is traced and shipped sideways: the base art in-game is rotated relative to how every photo viewer shows it. Preview and build agree, so the geometry is self-consistent, and the author sees the rotation on the canvas before Generate. A 16-bit greyscale PNG (mode I;16) converts to solid white.
findings.evidence: probe_doc.py section 8: an 800x400 JPEG with Orientation=6 gives 'img_size (800, 400)'. Section 9: 'mode I;16 -> RGB pixel (255, 255, 255)'.
findings.user_path: Open a portrait phone photo in the Trace tab. It appears sideways.
findings.fix: Add one shared _open_rgb(path) in imagefield that applies ImageOps.exif_transpose and normalises I;16/I modes, and use it at all four ingest sites (the Qt pixmap load must use the same transposed image).

findings.title: Composed-snip write and cut-out read errors escape their Qt slots silently
findings.statement: Writing the composed <stem>.fg{i}.png beside the source photo is deliberate. PLAN.md:136 says 'written beside the source image' so the emitted command stays re-runnable. The 'pollutes the photo folder' part is therefore by design, and a collision with a user file of that exact name is unlikely. The real part is error handling. frame.save() in _composed_fg_path (called from on_generate) and Image.open() in _attach_cutout (called from _on_contact and on_fg_attach) are not wrapped. A read-only photo folder, or a corrupt or unsupported PNG, raises inside a Qt slot. No sys.excepthook is installed in the workspace (grep: only worldforest.py references one), so under pythonw the traceback goes nowhere: Generate silently does not start, and the contact stays unattached after its history entry was pushed. Stale fgN files remain after a removal renumbers the indices.
findings.evidence: Code path read: tracedoc.py:840-841 -> _composed_fg_path:1119-1120 (no try); _attach_cutout:323 Image.open (no try), called at :774 and :790 after _push_history. grep for excepthook in workspace/ and apps/ff9_workspace.pyw found none beyond worldforest. PLAN.md:136 documents the write location. Not run end-to-end (it needs a read-only folder).
findings.user_path: Trace a photo from a read-only folder (for example a mounted share), place a snip and click Generate. Nothing happens and no message appears.
findings.fix: Wrap the attach and compose steps in try/except (OSError, PIL.UnidentifiedImageError) and report through self._refresh(msg, 'error'). Optionally fall back to <out>/src/ when the photo folder is not writable. Keep the documented location otherwise.

findings.title: Trace's 'next step' after Generate is an unquoted terminal command instead of the in-app Deploy
findings.statement: ok_next reads 'Deploy it: py tools/deploy_field.py <out>/<name>.field.toml --id N — then ~ → Warp to field → N'. Both premises are true. The path is unquoted, so it breaks when copied if the path has spaces: the installed default proj_base is ~/Dream World IX, and many home folders have spaces. tools/ exists only in a git checkout, while proj_base already switches on that case. Every comparable Workspace hint (importdoc's 'Build & Deploy → Deploy', the builddoc verdicts) points to the in-app deploy. One part of the suggested fix is unsound: 'Press Deploy (F9) — then Warp to field → {fid}' is wrong when the Build tab's destination is a test slot. F9 runs build_deploy.on_go with the configured radio, and the test slot overrides the field's own id. The hint should defer to the deploy verdict for the warp id, since builddoc's own ok_next already names the right id.
findings.evidence: I read tracedoc.py:56-57 and :859-860, the other ok_next strings (grep across workspace/*.py: importdoc 794/1064 say 'Build & Deploy'), shell._deploy_now at 8391-8405, and the builddoc rb_test/rb_own radios at 182/196.
findings.user_path: Pip-installed Workspace > Trace > Generate > the Problems verdict says to run py tools/deploy_field.py with an unquoted path under 'Dream World IX'.
findings.fix: ok_next = 'It opened in the Editor — press Deploy (F9); the deploy verdict names the warp id.' For a checkout, keep a quoted terminal line (subprocess.list2cmdline) as a secondary hint, if at all.

findings.title: The canvas never refits on resize: adding the first cut-out (or any layout shrink) leaves cropped art and a scrollbar
findings.statement: BackdropCanvas fits only on a refit=True set_backdrop, deferred to the first paint, or on Ctrl+0. resizeEvent only re-pins the hint. The Trace cut-out strip is hidden until the first contact exists, so marking the first cut-out inserts a row and shrinks the canvas by about 40-55 px at the old zoom. A vertical scrollbar appears and the bottom of the floor (vertices 2/3, the contact label) goes off-screen. This happens every time, in every theme and scale. Window or splitter resizes behave the same way: a grown window keeps the small fit, and a shrunk one crops. No study doc records 'no refit on resize' as a decision; the only zoom contract is 'a same-field re-render keeps the user's zoom'. Ctrl+0 recovers, but it is advertised only in the pill. No data is affected.
findings.evidence: Viewed review-ctp/mist-100/trace-contacts_mist_100.png: vertical scrollbar at the right, floor running off the bottom, vertices 2/3 not visible. trace-ux-look/probe1.out: '[traced] viewport 706x359 vbar False fully-visible True' -> '[contact added] viewport 694x318 vbar True fully-visible False'. backdrop-code/probe1.py rerun: shrink resize from fit -> 'hbar=True(0..28) vbar=True(0..134)', with no refit.
findings.user_path: Trace: trace a floor, then switch to Cut-outs and mark a contact. The canvas gets shorter and the art is cropped with a scrollbar.
findings.fix: Track _at_fit (set by _fit, cleared by wheel zoom, Ctrl+1 and a hand pan). In resizeEvent, re-run _fit while _at_fit is true, measured from maximumViewportSize() so it cannot feed back. Separately, consider reserving the strip's row so it does not shrink the canvas.

findings.title: The pitch slider's dashed horizon is off-frame at the default pitch and for 23 of 43 positions
findings.statement: The pitch tooltip says to 'slide until the dashed horizon sits on the image's own eye level', and the empty-trace teach says to click 'below the dashed horizon'. With the session rig (distance 3000, fov 42) the horizon is inside the 448 px frame only for pitches 6-25 (y 175 down to 6). At the default 26 it sits at y=-4, just above the frame, so _draw_horizon draws nothing and the readout says 'horizon above the frame'. The same holds for every pitch from 26 to 48. A first-time user at the default sees no line, is told to click below one, and gets no direction cue. With PITCH_BAND's floor of 6, the horizon also can never sit lower than y≈175, so a photo whose eye line is mid-frame cannot be matched. The band's lower limit may be deliberate: PLAN notes low-pitch unsoundness in frame_floor.
findings.evidence: Computed cam.horizon_canvas_y(guide.make_camera(p, 3000, fov_x_deg=42)) for p in 6..48: 20 of 43 are inside 0..447, the default 26 gives -4. backdrop.py:377 returns without drawing when the horizon is off-frame. Every trace snap reads '26° · horizon above the frame'.
findings.user_path: Open an image in Trace at the default pitch.
findings.fix: When off-frame, say how far ('horizon 4 px above the frame') and draw a ghost tick or arrow at the top edge. Reword the empty-state teach so it does not presume a visible line. Optionally lower the default pitch so the line starts visible.

findings.title: Disabled ToolStrip segments (#railSeg) are pixel-identical to enabled ones
findings.statement: Before an image is open, tracedoc disables the Cut-outs and Regions segments (tracedoc.py:384-385), and Place disables both of its tools on refusal. ToolStrip segments reuse the #railSeg QSS, which has no :disabled rule. The generic QToolButton:disabled rule could not help anyway: it sets color $muted, the same colour an enabled UNCHECKED rail segment already uses. So a disabled segment looks exactly like a clickable one, and clicking it does nothing with no explanation. The reporter's suggested '$disabled_fg' token does not exist in style.py, so the fix must pick a colour distinct from $muted.
findings.evidence: Read the reporter's toolstrip_bare_vs_traced.png: the Cut-outs and Regions segments are identical in the bare (disabled) and traced (enabled) rows. style.py:822-838 has no #railSeg:disabled rule. style.py:255 QToolButton:disabled uses $muted, the same as #railSeg's resting colour at 823.
findings.user_path: Open the Trace tab before opening an image and click Cut-outs or Regions.
findings.fix: Add 'QToolButton#railSeg:disabled { color: $text_subtle; background: transparent; }' (an existing dimmer token), placed after :checked, or scope it to the ToolStrip. Give the disabled segments a tooltip such as 'Open an image first'. Verify by pixel diff of the bare and traced snaps.

findings.title: Trace Regions tool hides the traced floor polygon, so doors are placed without the walkable edge
findings.statement: _draw_trace returns early unless trace or contact mode is on. Contact mode deliberately keeps the polygon visible but inert (per the set_contact_mode docstring), but region mode drops the floor outline, its vertex dots and the +48u outset ring entirely. A gateway is meant to sit at the walkable edge, which the author now has to remember or read off the photo. Nothing in the docs or tests records this as intended; it looks like an omission from the contact-mode carve-out.
findings.evidence: Code read: backdrop.py:846-849. Viewed review-ctp/mist-100/trace-regions-canvas_mist_100.png: no cyan floor polygon or outset ring, while trace-traced shows them.
findings.user_path: Trace: trace a floor, then switch to Regions. The outline disappears.
findings.fix: Change the guard to 'self._trace_mode or self._contact_mode or self._region_mode'. Handles are already non-grabbable outside trace mode (mark_grabbable is gated on _trace_mode), and press resolution for vertices is gated on _trace_mode.

findings.title: Generate does nothing, silently, while another job is running
findings.statement: run_job returns False and starts nothing when a QProcess is already running (shell.py:9325-9326). on_generate handles only 'if started:' and has no else branch, so the click produces no status change, toast or console line. By then any placed snip has already been composed and written beside the photo (_composed_fg_path is called while the argv is built). The World tab's teleport handles the same refusal with a status message (shell.py:9366).
findings.evidence: My probe /v-trace-tab/p_doc.py with run returning False: 'status changed: False | project: None'. I read shell.py:9318-9326 and tracedoc.py:856-869.
findings.user_path: Start a long Build or Deploy > switch to Trace > click Generate > nothing happens.
findings.fix: else: self._refresh('Another job is running — Generate after it finishes.', 'warn').

findings.title: Trace's event-message box is unlabeled, capped at 180 px, shows the text's tail, and its tooltip wrongly says the words are not in the file
findings.statement: With Regions + Event active, the next zone's message is a bare QLineEdit pre-filled with '...'. It has setMaximumWidth(180), no label or placeholder, and sits right after the 'Event' radio. After programmatic text it shows the tail of the line, ':reaks underfoot.' in the mist-100 regions snap. Its tooltip says 'the words live in this session, not in the file'. That is false: Generate passes each message through --event-zone into the generated field.toml's [[event]] (imagefield.py:1099-1100) and also records it in the .trace.json sidecar (tracedoc.py:899). Leaving the '...' default ships a literal ellipsis popup.
findings.evidence: tracedoc.py:177-183, 666 (message captured at draw), 849 (--event-zone argv), 899 (sidecar); imagefield.py:1099-1100 (emitted into [[event]]). A crop of mist-100/trace-regions_mist_100.png shows the box reading ':reaks underfoot.'.
findings.user_path: Trace > Regions > Event: look at the message box before drawing.
findings.fix: Add a 'Message' label buddy and a placeholder in place of the '...' default (keep the build-time fallback). Raise or drop the max width. Call setCursorPosition(0) after setText. Reword the tooltip: the words are written into the generated project and kept in its .trace.json.

findings.title: The cut-outs combo crams 4-5 facts into one entry and truncates the PNG/needs-PNG state
findings.statement: Each cut-out entry reads 'fg{i} @ (cx,cy) · z N · <png name> · snip'. The combo has a 260 px minimum and does not stretch (the fg row ends in addStretch), so the closed combo cuts the text with no ellipsis. At 100% it ends 'pillar_snip.|'. The two facts the user most needs, which PNG is attached or '⚠ needs its PNG', and snip vs full-frame, come last and are the first to go. The contact pixel and z are also already on the canvas label.
findings.evidence: A crop of mist-100/trace-contacts_mist_100.png shows 'fg0 @ (230,320) · z 1073 · pillar_snip.|' with empty space to the right of the row. Code tracedoc.py:204 (setMinimumWidth 260), 222 (stretch), 430-435 (entry text order).
findings.user_path: Trace > Cut-outs: mark a contact and attach a PNG.
findings.fix: Lead with the state ('fg0 · pillar_snip.png · snip' or 'fg0 · ⚠ needs its PNG'). Move the pixel and z to each item's tooltip. Give the combo stretch (addWidget(fg_box, 1)) and setSizeAdjustPolicy, or set ElideMiddle on its view.

findings.title: Trace has no 'Detect floor' seed though imagefield.auto_floor exists for exactly that
findings.statement: imagefield.auto_floor (numpy seeded region grow, refusal-biased, reasons point to the hand trace) is documented as 'a SEED the human refines in the tracer'. The retired HTML tracer was fed by `image-field --auto-floor --trace`. The project memory records the hallway lesson as 'the tracer seed IS the product': auto-floor cannot know where a field ends at a doorway, so its output is a starting polygon to drag.
