The Workspace Trace tab never calls auto_floor, so the GUI lost the seed the CLI tracer had and every user clicks the outline from scratch. PLAN's DRAWN-MESH LAW forbids the floorplan COMPOSER from inferring a mesh. It does not forbid a human-refined seed in Trace.
findings.evidence: grep finds no reference to auto_floor under workspace/. imagefield.py:600-615 docstring. Project memory project-ff9-image-to-field.md lines 114-130 (seed in the tracer, the hallway lesson). PLAN.md:429-434 (the law is about the composer).
findings.user_path: Trace: open a photo of a room with a uniform floor.
findings.fix: Add a 'Detect floor' button in the Floor cluster. It calls auto_floor(self._image, pitch=…, fov=self._fov, distance=self._distance) and commits the polygon (in canvas px) as ONE undoable on_floor gesture. An ImageFieldError goes to the status line as a warn. Disable it with a tooltip when numpy is missing. Off the GUI thread if it is slow.

findings.title: Trace exposes no room-scale (distance) control or floor-size readout
findings.statement: The session owns _distance and _fov and passes them to the CLI (--distance/--fov). They are reset per new photo and restored on reopen, but the GUI shows them only as a readout when they differ from the default and offers no control. So an author cannot judge or change how large the traced floor will be relative to the party. The cheap, clearly valuable half is a status fragment with the traced floor's world bounding box (e.g. 'floor ≈ 2400×1800 u'). A distance spinner is more delicate: changing it rescales every un-projected vertex and contact, and a reopened project re-projects through it (the rung-7 'wrong camera' class), so it needs the same drift warning the pitch has.
findings.evidence: tracedoc.py:79-80, 272-274 (_camera uses _distance/_fov), 347-352 (readout only when non-default). PLAN.md:691-696 records the session-owned distance/fov fix.
findings.user_path: Trace a photo and wonder how big the room will be in-game.
findings.fix: First add the bounding-box readout from the trace's world points in _refresh. If a distance spin is added, re-feed set_backdrop(refit=False) as pitch does and reuse the _pitch_drift_note pattern for a reopened project.

findings.title: No user doc covers the Trace tab, and the docsite 'picture' card points to a different workflow and overclaims
findings.statement: The docsite card 'A field from a picture you painted' says 'trace the floor, let the kit solve the camera' and links Tutorial 03 (original-art field via `ff9mapkit new` plus guide painting with a chosen camera). Tutorial 03 never mentions image-field or the Trace tab, and Trace does not solve the camera: the user sets pitch by eye. Nothing under ff9mapkit/docs documents the Trace tab, cut-outs/contacts/snips, regions on a photo, the .trace.json reopen or the in-place Regenerate. ff9mapkit/README.md only lists `image-field` among commands.
findings.evidence: A case-insensitive grep over ff9mapkit/docs, docsite and README for 'Trace tab|image-field|trace.json' hits only README.md:67. Tutorial 03 mentions only 'trace-over' paint templates (line 39). Read what-can-i-do.md:243-249.
findings.user_path: A user following the docsite card to make a field from a photo.
findings.fix: Write a short 'A field from a photo — the Trace tab' tutorial (open, pitch, trace, cut-outs, regions, Generate, Deploy, reopen). Point the card at it and change 'solve the camera' to 'match the camera pitch'.

findings.title: Trace's 'Load <open field>' offer does not follow tree selection while the Trace tab is showing
findings.statement: _on_select live-feeds Behavior, Cutscene and Place when they are the current tab, but has no branch for Trace. offer_project is called only from _on_tab_changed (shell.py:5001-5005). Selecting a campaign member row while Trace is showing does not leave the tab: _open_editor mounts the form without setCurrentWidget. So the offer button keeps naming, and on click loads, the previously selected field, and a pristine tab does not auto-load the newly selected project. The impact is small: the label names the field, and switching tabs away and back refreshes it.
findings.evidence: I read shell.py:4862-4882 (only behavior_doc, cutscene_doc and place_doc are fed), 5001-5005 (the only offer_project call), 5093-5102 (_behavior_target follows the tree selection) and _open_editor at 5668 (no tab switch). I did not build a two-member campaign for a live probe; the code path is unambiguous.
findings.user_path: Open a campaign > show the Trace tab > select a different member in the tree > the offer button still names the earlier member.
findings.fix: Add the same live-follow branch: if self.tabs.currentWidget() is self.trace_doc, call trace_doc.offer_project(self.member_paths.get(self._behavior_target())).

findings.title: A cut-out PNG named '@2x' previews at half size (main Trace and Place art are immune)
findings.statement: BackdropCanvas scales pixmaps with QTransform.fromScale(w/pm.width(), h/pm.height()). A QPixmap loaded from a file named 'x@2x.png' gets devicePixelRatio 2, so its item is drawn at half the logical size. The mechanism is real, but the claim overstates where it reaches. The main Trace art goes through PIL cover-crop and then QPixmap.loadFromData (tracedoc.py:504-516), which never applies the @2x rule. Place art always comes from app-named files ('.place_backdrop.png' and 'real_<id>_cam<n>.png', placedoc.py:340/365). So the backdrop path at line 353 is unreachable with DPR 2, and no traced vertex is ever misregistered against the main art. The reachable case is a user-attached cut-out PNG whose filename ends in '@2x' (tracedoc.py:328 QPixmap(str(path))). A snip previews at half its rect, and a registered full-frame cut-out fills a quarter of the frame. Its base then no longer sits on the contact anchor, which is computed from the PIL size. The build uses the real file size, so the user positions the snip against a wrong-size preview, and the saved offset is off relative to what ships.
findings.evidence: Re-ran backdrop-code/probe4.py on the native platform: 'room@2x.png dpr 2.0 -> art scene rect (0,0,192,224)' and 'snip @2x rect want (40,300,60,50) got (40,300,30,25)'. The probe is valid for the canvas, but it feeds set_backdrop a file-loaded pixmap, which no host does. Code read: tracedoc.load_image uses loadFromData (DPR 1); placedoc builds the backdrop paths itself; only tracedoc._attach_cutout loads a user-named file.
findings.user_path: Trace > Cut-outs: mark a contact, then attach a PNG whose name ends in '@2x.png'. The snip or full-frame overlay previews at half or quarter size.
findings.fix: In tracedoc._attach_cutout, call f['pm'].setDevicePixelRatio(1) after loading (or load via QImageReader/PIL). Defensively, also scale by item.boundingRect() in backdrop.py:353/457/461. Add a fence that attaches a '@2x' file.

findings.title: The backdrop hint pill drifts off its corner after any scroll/pan (no scrollContentsBy re-pin)
findings.statement: The '_hint' and '_coords' labels are child widgets of the viewport. QGraphicsView scrolls by QWidget::scroll on the viewport, which moves those children, and BackdropCanvas re-pins them only in resizeEvent, _style_hint and _update_coords. After a scrollbar move or a hand-drag pan of a zoomed view, the pill slides with the content, up to the opposite corner. It snaps back on the next resize or vertex drag. floorplandoc.py:949 already fixed the identical bug with a scrollContentsBy override and a comment recording the owner-visible symptom. behaviordoc.StageCanvas (the Cutscene stage) creates the same viewport-child labels and has no scrollContentsBy either. I did not probe it, but it uses the same pattern. The pill is mouse-transparent, so the effect is visual: it ends up covering arbitrary art.
findings.evidence: Re-ran backdrop-code/probe1.py (native, WA_DontShowOnScreen, 641x561 and 640x560). 'after scroll to max ... hint=(62,61) want=(377,518)' and 'hint=(60,61) want=(376,517)'. Setting the scrollbar value is exactly what ScrollHandDrag does, so the probe is valid. grep: scrollContentsBy exists only in floorplandoc.py.
findings.user_path: Trace or Place canvas: Ctrl+scroll in until scrollbars appear, then drag-pan. The 'Ctrl+scroll zooms...' pill travels with the art.
findings.fix: Port floorplandoc's override: def scrollContentsBy(self, dx, dy): super().scrollContentsBy(dx, dy); self._place_hint(). Do the same in behaviordoc.StageCanvas. Fence it with a viewport-event pan at odd and even widths.

findings.title: A drag whose left-release is lost keeps following buttonless hover and commits on the next click
findings.statement: mouseMoveEvent drives any live _drag without checking event.buttons(), and only a LeftButton release ends it. The viewport has mouse tracking on (AnchorUnderMouse enables it; see the workspace SKILL), so buttonless moves really are delivered. If the left release is lost, for example by right-clicking a vertex mid-drag (which opens the modal 'Delete vertex' QMenu) and dismissing the menu, the vertex keeps following the cursor with the coords chip up. The next ordinary click then commits it at that stray spot through on_floor, which is undoable. The region sub-claim does not hold with the real hosts. Rotating a region via the right-click menu mid-drag emits region_changed, and both tracedoc._on_region_changed and placedoc._on_region_changed synchronously re-feed set_regions. That runs _rebuild, which clears _drag, so the later release cannot emit an unrotated overwrite. The overwrite only appears on a bare canvas with no host. The trigger (right-click while holding left, or a focus steal mid-drag) is rare.
findings.evidence: Re-ran probe2.py section A on the native platform: 'after a BUTTONLESS move: drag still live = True' and 'next click elsewhere committed: (216.4, 300.2) (vertex 0 was (150,250))'. My own probe v-canvas/pE.py (rotate emitted mid corner-drag, no host) gave 2 emissions, the second unrotated. Code read shows both hosts call _refresh_regions -> set_regions -> _rebuild (_drag=None) on region_changed, so a real host never sees the second emission. The lost release under a real QMenu grab was not reproduced headless.
findings.user_path: Trace Floor tool: press on a vertex, drag, right-click while still holding left, Esc the menu, release, then move the mouse. The vertex follows; clicking elsewhere commits it there.
findings.fix: In mouseMoveEvent, if self._drag and not (event.buttons() & Qt.LeftButton), cancel the drag (restore it via _rebuild). Ignore contextMenuEvent while _drag is set. Optionally cancel on focusOutEvent.

findings.title: Ctrl+wheel zoom ignores the delta magnitude, and a horizontal (y=0) Ctrl+wheel zooms out
findings.statement: Each Ctrl+wheel event applies a full 1.15x step regardless of angleDelta size. A hi-res wheel or precision touchpad that splits one 120 detent into many small deltas zooms about 3x per detent instead of 1.15x. A Ctrl+wheel event with angleDelta().y()==0 (tilt wheel or sideways swipe) fails the '> 0' test and zooms out. The same three-line block is copied in floorplandoc.py:975, behaviordoc.py:314 and mapview.py:612. There is no shared helper; it is four copies.
findings.evidence: probe1.py rerun (QWheelEvent sent to the viewport, a valid emulation): 'ctrl + 8x15: zoom 1.0261 -> 3.1389 (x3.059)' and 'ctrl + HORIZONTAL wheel: zoom 1.1800 -> 1.0261'. grep confirms the identical code in the three other views.
findings.user_path: Ctrl + two-finger scroll on a precision touchpad over the Trace/Place/Cutscene canvas, or Ctrl + tilt-wheel.
findings.fix: dy = event.angleDelta().y(); if dy == 0: accept and return; f = 1.15 ** (dy / 120). Ideally hoist it into one helper used by all four views.

findings.title: Snips and contact diamonds show the Move cursor in Trace's Regions tool, where a press does not drag them
findings.statement: mark_grabbable is applied to every unlocked snip (line 467) and every contact glyph (line 485) in every mode, but press resolution drags them only in trace or contact mode (line 1122). In the Trace tab's Regions tool, hovering an attached snip or its contact diamond shows SizeAll, while a press pans, starts a region-corner click, or grabs an underlying quad. Place never feeds cut-outs (set_cutouts is called only by tracedoc), so the reachable case is Trace > Regions alone, not 'any place-mode host'. The vertex dots already gate their cursor on _trace_mode.
findings.evidence: probe2.py section F rerun: cutoutimg and cutoutpt-child cursors are SizeAllCursor in region mode; 'press on the snip in region mode -> drag armed: False', 'cutout_moved: []'. grep: set_cutouts is called only in tracedoc.py:463/526.
findings.user_path: Trace: attach a snip, switch to Regions, hover the snip (Move cursor), drag. It pans or places a corner instead.
findings.fix: Wrap both mark_grabbable calls in 'if self._trace_mode or self._contact_mode', matching the press gate.

findings.title: Esc does not abort a live vertex/corner/snip drag (the double-click half is mostly harmless)
findings.statement: keyPressEvent handles Esc only for a pending region quad. During a vertex, corner, quad, snip or contact drag, Esc does nothing and the release still commits, so the only way back is Undo. That half is confirmed. The double-click half is overstated. QGraphicsView's mouseDoubleClickEvent does not route through mousePressEvent, so a press/release/dblclick/release sequence yields one vertex. But Qt raises a DblClick only when the second press lands within the platform double-click distance (a few px) and interval. Two quick clicks on different vertex or corner positions, which are normally far apart, are not merged. The dropped click is a near-duplicate point within ~5px, arguably a de-duplication rather than a lost vertex.
findings.evidence: probe2.py rerun. Section B: 'drag still live after Esc: True', 'commits after Esc+release: 1'. Section C: 'vertices after press/release/dblclick/release: 1', with the second click only 3px from the first, which is the only geometry that produces a DblClick.
findings.user_path: Trace: start dragging a vertex, press Esc, release. The move is committed anyway.
findings.fix: In keyPressEvent: if Esc and self._drag, set _drag=None, hide the coords chip, _rebuild() (restores the start state), and accept. Leave the double-click alone, or treat a DblClick as a press only if testing shows real loss.

findings.title: A whole-quad drag that tracedoc refuses (corner behind the camera) leaves the un-accepted quad drawn
findings.statement: After a changed corner or quad drag, _end_vertex_drag emits region_changed and does not rebuild, relying on the host to re-feed. tracedoc._on_region_changed returns early without _refresh_regions when world_to_click raises. This happens when a whole-quad drag moves a deep zone far enough toward the camera that its near corners go behind the camera plane. The canvas then keeps the moved, never-accepted polygon and handles, with no status message, while the document holds the old quad. Its law overlays stay hidden if it had any. The extension to snip and contact drags does not hold: tracedoc._on_cutout_moved and _on_contact_moved always refresh for reachable inputs, and placedoc's handler always refreshes.
findings.evidence: v-canvas/p10.py (native): a 2100-unit-deep event zone grabbed near its far edge and dragged to the frame bottom emitted [(-302,-3649),(298,-3649),(298,-1549),(-302,-1549)]. world_to_click REFUSED the two near corners ('at/behind the camera plane'), which is exactly tracedoc.py:681-682's silent return path. Code read of the other handlers.
findings.user_path: Trace > Regions: drag a long zone by its far end down to the bottom of the frame and release. The quad stays drawn where it was dropped, but the document did not change.
findings.fix: Always _rebuild() after emitting region_changed (a host that accepts re-feeds anyway), and/or make tracedoc refuse with _refresh_regions() plus a status message instead of a bare return.

findings.title: Backdrop tests are offscreen at one size and never exercise pan/zoom/fit, hint pinning, lost releases or DPR-2
findings.statement: test_workspace_backdrop.py sets QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen and builds every canvas at 500x560. There is no test for Ctrl+wheel, Ctrl+0/Ctrl+1, fit-after-zoom, resize refit, hint position after scroll, buttonless-move drag termination, Esc mid-drag, double-click or a DPR-2 pixmap. The only Escape test covers the pending-region case. Every view-grammar defect confirmed in this batch (V2, V4, V5, V3, T24) passes the 36 green tests. The workspace SKILL itself requires odd/even parametrized view fences and at least one sendEvent-driven fence per canvas.
findings.evidence: py -m pytest tests/test_workspace_backdrop.py -q -p no:cacheprovider -> '36 passed'. grep finds no wheel, Key_0, scroll, _fit or DPR assertions; the only Key_Escape is at line 585 (pending quad). The SKILL.md 'Parity is the gate' section mandates odd and even fences.
findings.user_path: n/a (test suite)
findings.fix: Add a native WA_DontShowOnScreen fixture parametrized at (641,561)/(640,560) covering: pan -> hint geometry; zoom then Ctrl+0 equals the first fit; Ctrl+wheel 8x15 equals one 1.15 step; a buttonless move after a lost release does not move a vertex; Esc mid-drag restores.

findings.title: An invalid trace vertex differs from a good one only by colour; region-law detail is tooltip-only
findings.statement: A vertex above the horizon is drawn with the same dot and index label as a valid one, differing only in colour (error vs accent), and its reason is a hover tooltip. The DEAD ZONE / OVER-TRIGGER percentages exist only as tooltips on the painted hatch and wash, and Place's status literally says '(hover a marked quad)'. Some non-colour cues do exist. Tracedoc's status line counts 'N above the horizon (red)' and gates Generate with a tooltip, and warned regions carry a '⚠' glyph in their label and an '⚠ N with law warnings' status count. The status line just never says which vertex or what the law detail is. The '<1.6:1 on the tan floor' figure depends on the user's photo and cannot be checked as a general claim. The canvas has no keyboard operation at all, so the practical beneficiary is a colour-vision-deficient mouse user.
findings.evidence: Code read: backdrop.py:865-884 (colour-only bad vertex plus tooltip), 595-609 (gap/spill tooltips), 650 ('⚠ ' label prefix for warned regions), tracedoc.py:394-411 (status counts), placedoc.py:897 ('hover a marked quad').
findings.user_path: Trace: pitch the camera so one vertex goes above the horizon. Only its red colour marks it.
findings.fix: Draw a bad vertex hollow or with an ✕ and suffix its label ('3 ✕'). Have the status line name the offending vertex indices. Mirror the selected or warned region's law text into the status line instead of 'hover a marked quad'.

findings.title: Retheme/scale tests only check attribute assignment; several real states (horizon in frame, multi-cam, stacked chooser, drift) have no snap
findings.statement: test_retheme_and_scale_reach_the_canvas asserts only 'doc.canvas.pal is doc.pal' and 'canvas._scale == 150'. It would stay green if _rebuild ignored the scale or the palette when painting labels. test_retheme_and_set_scale_survive_both_pages (test_cutscenedoc.py:773) checks the slider's minimum width and the crumb. gui_snap has no state for a horizon inside the frame. TRACE_STATES' docstring promises 'the bare canvas frame with its horizon', but the default 26° pitch puts the horizon above the frame: the snaps read '26° · horizon above the frame' and the horizon line and its label appear in no snap. There is also no multi-camera Place state, no stacked-floor _choose_hit, no pitch-drift/offer state and no Cutscene problems state.
findings.evidence: Read test_workspace_tracedoc.py:178-183 and test_cutscenedoc.py:773-779. grep tools/gui_snap.py for cam_box/_choose_hit/unresolved/_pitch_drift/offer finds nothing. Snap mist-100/trace-contacts shows '26° · horizon above the frame'; probe5 shows horizon_canvas_y = -3.66 at 26°.
findings.user_path: n/a (test and snap coverage)
findings.fix: After set_scale/retheme, assert a painted label item's font().pointSize() and brush colour. Add gui_snap states trace:horizon (pitch about 12) and place:multicam at least, and fix the TRACE_STATES 'bare' docstring.

findings.title: An add lane started at row 0 never re-enables 'Runs with the previous beat'
findings.statement: _sync_with_prev runs only from _on_kind. When the add lane opens at row 0 (only when the scene has no steps), the checkbox is correctly disabled. After Apply advances insert_at to 1, the checkbox is never re-synced, so it stays disabled for a parallel-capable kind until the author toggles the step type. The case is narrow because a row-0 add lane needs an empty scene.
findings.evidence: Re-ran p11_editor_misc.py: 'add lane now at row 1 | with_prev enabled: False' for a turn. Grep: _sync_with_prev is called only at cutscenedoc.py:379, inside _on_kind.
findings.user_path: Delete every step, press Add, Apply a turn at row 0, then try to tick with_prev for row 1.
findings.fix: Call self.editor._sync_with_prev() after advancing insert_at in _apply_step's add branch.

findings.title: The build reports a bad cutscene tail twice, once without the dispatch index
findings.statement: For a cast scene in a [[cutscene]] dispatch, an invalid step tail produces two messages: one from the window-attribute sweep (build.py:3236, labelled '[cutscene] step 0', with no '#k' even when there are several blocks) and one from _validate_conductor (build.py:9054-9056, labelled '[cutscene] #0 step 0'). Check therefore shows a duplicate, and the sweep's label is ambiguous in a dispatch. The same missing-'#k' problem affects every other sweep message on cutscene steps, such as an unknown style.
findings.evidence: p5_problems_parity.py 'bad tail code' BUILD: ["[cutscene] step 0 tail 'XYZ' is not a valid TAIL code (DEFT, ...)", "[cutscene] #0 step 0 tail 'XYZ' is not a valid TAIL code"]. Read the sweep at build.py:3230-3238, which labels f"[cutscene] step {_sk}" and ignores _ci.
findings.user_path: A dispatch whose cast scene has a say with tail = "XYZ": the Check output lists it twice.
findings.fix: Drop the conductor's tail check (the sweep covers every text step), and have the sweep label '[cutscene] #k step n' when there are several blocks.

findings.title: '− Scene' deletes immediately (undo-first by design); the real risk is the elided label
findings.statement: The premise is true: '− Scene' runs _del_scene with no confirmation, next to '⧉ Scene'. But delete-without-confirm plus Ctrl+Z is this surface's deliberate contract. The tooltip says 'Ctrl+Z undoes; the file changes on Save, not now', the step ✕ follows the same rule, and the shell checkpoints the edit with the op's label (_on_cutscene_edit). Nothing is lost until Save. The part that is a real defect, both buttons reading 'Sce…', belongs to C17 and goes away with that fix. Adding a confirm dialog would contradict the house undo-first pattern. A status-bar note naming what was removed is the only worthwhile addition.
findings.evidence: probe_flows.py: '4. scenes before/after one click on - Scene: 2 1'. Code: tooltip at line 787. _on_cutscene_edit (shell.py ~5044) records a checkpoint. The step delete (line 597 tooltip 'Remove this step (Ctrl+Z undoes)') uses the same no-confirm, undo-backed idiom.
findings.user_path: Click '− Scene'.
findings.fix: Fix C17 (the labels). Optionally post a transient status message with the checkpoint label ('Deleted scene #0 (3 steps) — Ctrl+Z restores'). Do not add a modal confirm.

findings.title: 'Pick on the stage' stays armed after the step kind changes away from walk or teleport
findings.statement: _on_kind hides pick_btn for non-movement kinds but never disarms the host's one-shot stage pick. The canvas stays in sim-click mode, and the next click on the stage writes 'x, z' into the now-hidden value line. That stale coordinate then appears if the author switches to another line-valued kind, for example Wait shows '123, 457', and an Apply would fail or carry it.
findings.evidence: My probe v-cutscene-bugs/pick.py, using public gestures (kind combo plus pick_btn.click()): 'armed: True', after switching to say 'armed: True pick visible-flag: False', and after a stage click 'hidden value_line now: '123, 457''; switching to wait shows '123, 457'.
findings.user_path: Step editor on a walk: Pick on the stage, change Type to Say without clicking the stage, then click the stage later (for example to pan or select).
findings.fix: Add an on_kind_changed hook so the host can call _disarm_stage_pick when the new kind is not walk or teleport. Optionally show an 'armed' state on the button.

findings.title: '+speaker' extras chip hides the speaker's name and reads like an add button
findings.statement: A step with extra keys shows a right-aligned info chip '+speaker' (or '+speaker, tail'). The ladder shows an actor chip only for `actor`, so a conversation authored with `speaker` never shows who is talking in the ladder. The chip only names the key, behind a '+' that reads like an action. It is passive and does nothing on click. The useful half (the name) is worth surfacing.
findings.evidence: Read mist-100/cutscene-doc-pane: row 2 'say Made it to the altar.' with a '+speaker' pill in the same slot as '‖ with previous'. Code lines 609-627.
findings.user_path: Any say step that has speaker = '…'.
findings.fix: Show the speaker as the row's name chip (e.g. 'Cid' in the actor slot, with distinct styling if an actor is also set) and the remaining extras as a muted caption without the '+'.

findings.title: '(no line this beat)' placeholder is the loudest text in the storyboard strip
findings.statement: board_say is a mono QLabel. On a beat with no say line it shows '(no line this beat)' at full label size in heavy monospace, visually heavier than the scene title, while the explanatory ledger below is a small caption. An empty-state placeholder should be quiet.
findings.evidence: Read mist-150/cutscene-storyboard_mist_150.png: '(no line this beat)' in large bold mono under the slider dominates 'scene #0'. Code line 1432 sets the text with no state or role change.
findings.user_path: ▶ Storyboard on a scene whose first beat is a walk.
findings.fix: When b['say'] is None, set the caption role or a muted state on board_say (and restore it for a real line), or hide board_say and show the placeholder in the ledger line.

findings.title: Some engine identifiers in Settings help and an ambiguous 'run Check'
findings.statement: The premise is true: the front door says "Cutscene stages a field's [[cutscene]] scenes", the CUTSCENE_SPEC help says 'the DIRECTOR GATE: only plays when the ScenarioCounter == this beat', 'the DIRECTOR ADVANCE' and 'pin THIS gEventGlobal bit', and the staging summary says '(unresolved names — run Check)' right beside a button titled 'Check the staging'. Only part of it is worth changing. TOML block names such as [[npc]] and [[cutscene]] are the kit's shared vocabulary across docs, the 'Open the .toml' door and the Editor tree. CUTSCENE_SPEC is also the Editor tab's form for the same block, so it is not a first-time-only path. The worthwhile changes: rewrite the ScenarioCounter/gEventGlobal/DIRECTOR help into plain words, keeping the engine term second or in the '?' badge, and make 'run Check' name the toolbar Check, which is a different action from Check the staging.
findings.evidence: Read forms.py:259-279 and cutscenescan.py:58 ('NOT checked (unresolved names — run Check)'). The instrument column's button reads 'Check the staging' (cutscenedoc.py:914). The toolbar has a separate 'Check' (visible in snaps).
findings.user_path: Open Scene settings; or run Check the staging on a scene with a typo'd marker.
findings.fix: Plain-language help ('only plays once the story has reached this point (number or area name); blank = always'), with the engine name as a second line or in the badge. Change 'run Check' to 'run the toolbar Check'. Leave the [[block]] names.

findings.title: First-run banner says 'Your fork is ready' for any field, including a from-scratch one
findings.statement: The first-run spine message is hardcoded as 'Your fork is ready — press Deploy to put it in your game.' whenever prefs.has_deployed() is false, whatever the member's origin. A standalone authored field (the status bar says 'GLEN — standalone field') is described as a fork.
findings.evidence: Read shell.py:8363-8367: no branch on origin. Every cutscene window snap shows the banner beside 'GLEN — standalone field'. No test or doc pins the string (grepped tests/, docs, docsite).
findings.user_path: First launch, open or create a loose field without forking.
findings.fix: Say 'Your field is ready — press Deploy…' (true for both cases), or branch on whether the member came from import/fork.

findings.title: Rowtools are 20-23px tall (below the house 24px floor); boundary ↑/↓ are enabled no-ops
findings.statement: Measured natively at 100%, the five per-row tools are 21x23, 28x23, 29x23 and 34x20 (the pencil), below the 24px floor that test_workspace_a11y.py:110 enforces for stock controls. That fence never measures role=rowtool. ↑ on row 0 and ↓ on the last row are enabled but silently return (cutscenedoc.py:1271), which wastes a tab stop. The 'WCAG 2.5.8 violation' framing is overstated: 2.5.8 has a spacing exception, and with 7px row spacing between tool centres (≥28px apart) a 24px circle around each target does not overlap its neighbours. So this is a house-rule miss, not a WCAG failure.
findings.evidence: probe_kb.py: 'rowtools 15 sizes [(21, 23), (28, 23), (29, 23), (34, 20)]', 'up on step0 enabled: True'. style.py:183/190 rowtool_pad '1px 6px' and '0px 5px'. The test at test_workspace_a11y.py:110-130 builds only stock controls.
findings.user_path: Mouse or keyboard use of the ladder row tools.
findings.fix: Add min-height: 24px; min-width: 24px to QPushButton[role="rowtool"] (this also covers the behavior ladder, which shares the role). Disable ↑ on row 0 and ↓ on the last row in StepLadder._row, which needs the row count. Add a rowtool button to the target-size fence.

findings.title: Regions status reads 'draw a event zone' and teaches the gateway walk-out edge in Event mode; rotate is undone as 'reshape gateway zone'
findings.statement: The status line builds 'Click 4 corners to draw a {kind} zone', which gives 'a event'. It always appends 'corners 0→1 = a gateway's walk-out edge', even while drawing events. The walk-out rotate goes through move_zone, so its undo and redo label is the generic 'reshape gateway zone', the same as a corner drag or a body drag.
findings.evidence: Probe probes/x-cutscene-place/p5_place.py: final status 'Click 4 corners to draw a event zone · 2 regions · corners 0→1 = a gateway's walk-out edge …'; undo labels ['draw gateway door0 -> 0', 'retarget door0 -> 4005', 'reshape gateway zone', 'reshape gateway zone', 'reshape gateway zone'] for retarget, rotate, corner drag and body drag.
findings.user_path: Place → Regions → Event; or right-click a gateway → Walk-out edge → read the Undo label
findings.fix: Use 'an event'/'a gateway', show the walk-out sentence only in gateway mode, and give the rotate its own label ('rotate walk-out edge of door0').

findings.title: Fully degenerate zones (collinear / all-coincident corners) get no region-law warning
findings.statement: imagefield.zone_fan_audit returns gap=0 and spill=0 for a zero-area quad, so region_rows shows no warning for a trigger that can never fire. Four collinear corners and four coincident corners both pass clean. The claim's second example is overstated: a single corner dragged onto another (one collapsed edge) still produces a ~3% over-trigger warning. RUNG6.md:32 already records that the audit is 'vacuous on degeneracy', but Place never added a guard. Drawing four collinear clicks by hand is unlikely, so this is polish.
findings.evidence: My probe v-place-bugs/p_misc.py: collinear {'gap':0,'spill':0} warn: None; all-same warn: None; collapsed [[0,0],[0,0],[100,100],[0,100]] warn: 'over-trigger ~3%'. RUNG6.md line 32 documents the vacuity.
findings.user_path: Regions -> four clicks in a line, or drag corners onto each other until the quad has no area.
findings.fix: In region_rows, warn when the shoelace area of the stored integer quad is below a small floor (for example under one character footprint, ~100x100).

findings.title: All placed-content markers share one ring glyph regardless of kind
findings.statement: content_markers carries kind (npc/prop/chest/spawn/arrival) and _refresh_markers passes it to the canvas, but _draw_markers ignores it and draws the same ring, dot and label for everything. Kind can only be read from the label text, and labels overprint where markers cluster: in place-fork at 150% the 'Mira' label sits under prop0's marker and column.
findings.evidence: backdrop.py:420-439 never reads m['kind']. placedoc.py:877 passes kind through. mist-150/place-fork_mist_150.png shows 'Mira' and 'prop0' as identical rings with overlapping labels.
findings.user_path: Place several kinds of content close together.
findings.fix: Choose the glyph by kind in _draw_markers: ring for npc, square for prop, box for chest, triangle for spawn, diamond with its entrance number for arrival.

findings.title: gui_snap's Place fixtures mis-register the walkmesh on the art and stage an unreachable 'refused' screen
findings.statement: The 'fork' and 'regions' states pair the test_imagefield painted room with an unrelated make_camera(26, 3000) and a flat 1800x2100 quad (z 500..2600). In the snaps the footprint trapezoid covers only the back sliver of the painted floor, so every marker and zone crowds at the horizon. A reviewer cannot judge overlay registration, and part of P21's crowding is a fixture artefact. The 'refused' state calls place_doc.show_field directly without win.open_field, so the window shows 'Nothing open yet' in the tree, an empty Inspector and a 'Open a journey…' status bar, while Place claims 'hut_int — donor field #351'. No user can reach that combination.
findings.evidence: Read gui_snap.py:1874-1917. Read mist-150/place-fork_mist_150.png (footprint at about y 820-885 display px against a floor painted to about 1100) and mist-100/place-refused_mist_100.png (tree 'Nothing open yet', Inspector empty).
findings.user_path: Reviewer-only: reading the place snaps.
findings.fix: Project the painted floor polygon (or build the camera _paint_room used) so the fixture tris match the art. For 'refused', open a temp copy through win.open_field with protected_reason pinned through a seam, or open the example read-only through the shell.

findings.title: Place's breadcrumb is the bare member name, unlike the Behavior and Cutscene tabs
findings.statement: PlaceDoc.crumb_label returns just the member name ('PLACEDEMO'), so the crumb bar reads like the Editor's field crumb. BehaviorDoc (1583) and CutsceneDoc (946) both prefix their surface ('Behavior — X', 'Cutscene — X'), so Place is the odd one out among the three fed per-field docs. The Trace half of the claim is weaker. Trace deliberately shows _content_crumbs because on show it offers the open field for a one-click reopen (shell.py:5001-5005), so naming that field is defensible. Giving Trace its own crumb is optional.
findings.evidence: placedoc.py:911-912 vs behaviordoc.py:1582-1583 and cutscenedoc.py:946-947. shell.py:4994-5005 shows how each tab sets its crumb.
findings.user_path: Switch between the Author tabs with a field open and read the crumb bar.
findings.fix: return f'Place — {self._member}' if self._member else 'Place'. Leave Trace as is, or label it with the session image name.

findings.title: Pitch is not part of the undo history, so Undo after a slider move takes back an earlier gesture
findings.statement: _on_pitch marks the session not stamped but pushes no history entry, and snapshots do not record pitch. Pressing Undo after moving the pitch therefore leaves the slider where it is and removes the last floor, cut-out or region gesture. That matches the Undo tooltip ('Take back the last vertex or cut-out gesture'), and the module docstring defines undo as a history of gesture snapshots. So this is consistent with the stated design rather than a bug. It can still surprise an author who expects the slider to go back, but the slider is a live preview the author can simply drag back, and the removed gesture comes back with one Redo-free re-click. Real but low value.
findings.evidence: trace-code/probe_doc.py section 3: 'pitch before 26 after set 40 + Undo: 40 floor []'. I read the tracedoc.py docstring at line 15 and the Undo tooltip at line 186.
findings.user_path: Trace tab > trace a floor > move Pitch > click Undo > the last vertex disappears and the pitch stays.
findings.fix: Optional: record pitch in the snapshot and push one entry per slider gesture (sliderReleased). On restore, block signals and call _on_pitch's refresh. At least name the scope in the Undo tooltip.

findings.title: Event message starting with '-' and no space breaks the CLI argv
findings.statement: TraceDoc passes '--event-zone' and '<message>@<pts>' as two argv items. When the message starts with '-' and contains no space (for example '-Stop!'), argparse reads the value as an option and exits with 'argument --event-zone: expected one argument'. The Generate then fails, loudly, in Output. A message with any space, or not starting with '-', parses fine. Other argv values (floor, gateway head, foreground path) cannot start with '-' in practice.
findings.evidence: Re-ran probe_argv.py: "'-Stop!' -> argparse SystemExit 2", "'--' -> SystemExit 2", "'Hello there' -> parsed".
findings.user_path: Set an event zone's message to '-Stop!' and Generate. Output shows an argparse error.
findings.fix: Emit '--event-zone=<value>' (and '--name=<value>'), which argparse never mistakes for an option. One-line change.

findings.title: An opaque cut-out PNG is accepted with no warning
findings.statement: _attach_cutout reads only the image size, and build_image_field converts every foreground to RGBA (imagefield.py:1058). An RGB or fully opaque photo-aspect PNG (for example an unedited copy of the photo) is accepted as a registered full-frame occluder. It then covers the whole background, and the actor, wherever the actor is behind the contact line. The preview would show the overlay, so an attentive author may notice, but a one-line alpha check at attach time is cheap and worth adding.
findings.evidence: Code read of tracedoc.py:316-337 (no alpha check) and imagefield.py:1058 (convert('RGBA'), which makes RGB fully opaque).
findings.user_path: Attach an un-erased copy of the photo as a cut-out and Generate. In-game the actor vanishes whenever it walks behind the contact line.
findings.fix: At attach, if the image has no alpha band or its alpha minimum is 255, add a warn teach note ('this PNG has no transparent pixels - it will hide the actor everywhere behind the contact').

findings.title: Trace has no canvas empty state and does not accept a dropped image
findings.statement: In the bare state the Trace canvas is an empty 384x448 frame with the 'click the floor' hint pill. The only teach is the muted 'Open an image to begin.' at the bottom. The shell's drop handler accepts only .toml/.dat/.json/.glb/.gltf (shell.py:7676), and neither TraceDoc nor BackdropCanvas implements drop, so dropping a photo does nothing. Meanwhile the tree says 'Nothing open yet', the Inspector is empty and the status bar says 'Open a journey, campaign, or field to begin.', none of which this self-contained tab needs.
findings.evidence: shell.py:7676-7695 (_DROP_SUFFIXES and the guard). No setAcceptDrops or dropEvent in tracedoc.py or backdrop.py. mist-100/trace-bare snaps.
findings.user_path: Open Trace fresh; drag a PNG onto it.
findings.fix: Paint a centred 'Open or drop a photo' prompt in the empty frame. setAcceptDrops on TraceDoc, accepting image suffixes and calling load_image, or route image suffixes from the shell to Trace.

findings.title: Trace lives on the Assets rail, away from Place/Floorplan; no Field ▸ New entry points to it
findings.statement: The premise is true. Trace is grouped under Assets (Import, Trace, Models, Battle) while Place and Floorplan, which share the BackdropCanvas and the Regions tool, are under Author. But the placement is a recorded, defensible choice (PLAN rung 1: 'on the Assets rail'). Import and Trace are the two ways to bring outside material in as a field, and Ctrl-K has 'Go to Trace (turn a photo into a field)'. A move is not warranted. The cheap, worthwhile part is discoverability from the New Field flow. (Code order is Import, Trace, Models, Battle, so Trace is not literally last.)
findings.evidence: shell.py:1841-1849 rail groups; shell.py:5275 Ctrl-K entry; PLAN.md:761 placement record.
findings.user_path: A newcomer looks under Author or the Field menu for 'make a field from a picture'.
findings.fix: Add a 'Trace a photo…' item beside New Field… in the Field menu that switches to the Trace tab. Optionally show a 'Place content on it' hint after the first Generate. Keep the rail as is.

findings.title: Trace's Inspector column is empty in every state
findings.statement: With Trace active, the right Inspector column (about a quarter of the window) shows only the 'Inspector' heading and its rule. Meanwhile the tab crams vertex counts, warnings and the project/stamp state into the one overflowing status line under the canvas (T23). Behavior and Cutscene already mount an instruments panel into the Inspector (_mount_behavior_instruments / _mount_cutscene_instruments), so the pattern exists. Moving the session summary there would also relieve T23.
findings.evidence: Pixel scan of the Inspector column (display x 1700-1990, y 240-1200) in mist-100 trace-traced and trace-contacts: 100% background. The same scan on cutscene-doc_mist_100: 96% background (instruments drawn). shell.py:4963-4964 mounts instruments for Behavior and Cutscene only.
findings.user_path: Any Trace session.
findings.fix: Add _mount_trace_instruments: image name, pitch/distance, vertex and cut-out/region counts with warnings, the generated project path, stamped vs not, and the deploy hint. Then shorten the status line.

findings.title: Ctrl+0 from a zoomed view fits ~2% small because it measures the scrollbar-reduced viewport
findings.statement: _fit computes the zoom from viewport().width()/height(), which shrink while the zoomed transform shows scrollbars. Ctrl+0 pressed from a zoomed view therefore fits to the smaller viewport. The scrollbars then disappear, leaving the art about 2% smaller and a few px off-centre compared with the first-paint fit in the same window. Further Ctrl+0 presses are stable, so it does not ratchet. The effect is cosmetic and barely visible.
findings.evidence: probe1.py rerun: first fit 'vp=637x557 m11=1.20600 dx=86'; after zoom-in (vp 625x545) Ctrl+0 gives 'vp=637x557 m11=1.18002 dx=91'. At 640x560: 1.20384 vs 1.17786.
findings.user_path: Ctrl+scroll in until scrollbars show, then press Ctrl+0.
findings.fix: Fit against maximumViewportSize() (independent of the current transform), or resetTransform() first, process the layout, then measure.

findings.title: Dragging a vertex above the horizon commits it, while a click there is refused (feedback does exist)
findings.statement: Appending a vertex refuses above the horizon (click_refused), but _end_vertex_drag commits the dragged canvas point unconditionally, so a drag can create a vertex the build would refuse. The asymmetry is real. The claim that 'the host status line gets no message' is wrong. on_floor -> tracedoc._on_floor -> _refresh writes 'N vertices traced · 1 above the horizon (red)'. Generate is disabled with a tooltip saying every vertex must be below the horizon, and the coords chip reads 'above the horizon' during the drag. The design already treats canvas px as truth and renders red vertices; the pitch-change case creates them too. So this is an inconsistency with visible feedback, not silent bad data, and undo reverts it.
findings.evidence: probe5.py rerun: 'committed: (150.1, -43.9) click_refused: [] worlds: None'. Code read: tracedoc.py:549-552 (_on_floor -> _refresh), 394-395 (status note counts red vertices), 358-380 (Generate gated and tooltip).
findings.user_path: Trace: drag a vertex up past the horizon and release.
findings.fix: On release, if click_to_world(d['pt']) raises, emit click_refused(msg) and _rebuild() without committing, mirroring the region-corner drag that holds the corner below the horizon.

findings.title: Contact mode: clicking on an existing snip's opaque pixels arms a no-op snip drag instead of a contact
findings.statement: In contact mode, mousePressEvent resolves cutoutimg (alpha-masked) before falling through to the contact click. A slop click on an existing snip's opaque pixels therefore arms a snip drag that ends unchanged (no cutout_moved), and contact_clicked is never emitted. The Cut-outs tool stays armed and the status line says nothing. Marking a second object's base where it overlaps an attached snip gets no response. This is rare: the object's base must sit on top of another snip's opaque body.
findings.evidence: probe2.py section G rerun: 'contact_clicked after a slop click on the snip body: []'. Code read: tracedoc._on_contact is the only consumer.
findings.user_path: Trace > Cut-outs with one snip attached: click on the snip's opaque body to mark a new contact. Nothing happens.
findings.fix: In contact mode, skip arming snip drags (contact handles still re-anchor), or treat a cimg drag released within _CLICK_SLOP_PX as a contact click.

findings.title: Canvas handle radii are fixed px under the CALIBRE dial; the cut-out combo truncation is NOT a scale effect
findings.statement: _HANDLE_R=4 (an 8px handle), the 8px marker ring, the 10px contact diamond and the label offsets are constant screen px, while label fonts scale with the dial. At 150% the grab targets get relatively smaller next to the text, a polish issue. The supporting example is wrong. The fg_box cut-out combo truncates at 100% too ('fg0 @ (230,320) · z 1073 · pillar_snip.|' in mist-100/trace-contacts), and the row has free space to its right. So the truncation comes from the combo's own sizing (min width 260, no stretch, default AdjustToContentsOnFirstShow while the strip was hidden and empty), not from the 150% dial. tracedoc.set_scale only forwards to the canvas, so the px widths are never re-derived.
findings.evidence: Read the backdrop.py constants (48, 429, 481) and tracedoc.py:119/178/204/247/255 and set_scale at 1140. Viewed review-ctp/mist-100/trace-contacts_mist_100.png (truncated at 100%) and mist-150/trace-contacts_mist_150.png.
findings.user_path: Trace at 150% text size: vertex and corner handles stay 8px.
findings.fix: Optionally scale _HANDLE_R and the glyph sizes by self._scale/100 in _rebuild. Fix the combo separately (see the extra finding): give it a stretch factor or AdjustToContents rather than px math.

refuted_or_by_design.title: Trace's first Generate opens the project on the Editor tab, not Place
refuted_or_by_design.statement: The premise is accurate: on_generated is shell.open_field, which ends with tabs.setCurrentWidget(self.doc_scroll), so the author lands on the Field form. This is the recorded design, though. The _after_generate docstring and the pinning test test_first_generate_hands_the_project_to_the_shell_once both say a clean first Generate 'opens the project in the Editor (which is what feeds Place, 7d)'. 'One flow' means Place is already fed with the project, not that the author is moved to it. A one-line status hint pointing to Place would be a small improvement, but the behaviour is intended.

refuted_or_by_design.title: The missing eye in _px_to_zone_world's refine pass is not what puts a handle off the cursor
refuted_or_by_design.statement: The code asymmetry is real: line 523 calls floor_y_at without the eye, while _zone_y passes it. The claimed consequence does not follow from it. The refine branch runs only when the pixel's ray misses every walkmesh triangle. The refine then re-intersects the ray with the plane at the chosen floor's height y. If the triangle at height y contained that new (x', z'), the ray would have hit it, contradicting the miss (exactly so for flat floors). So the refined corner never lies on the floor that was picked, and _zone_y resolves its render height from other triangles or the nearest-vertex fallback whichever candidate the refine chose. The corner can sit off the cursor in this off-mesh case with or without the eye. Passing the eye is a harmless consistency tidy that fixes nothing user-visible.
